Deals · Joint ventures

# Buying out your Indian JV partner: pricing, filings and what to check first

More foreign groups are moving from 50:50 or 74:26 joint ventures in India to full ownership, helped by FDI caps that have opened up in sectors such as insurance. Buying the Indian partner’s stake is a share transfer from a resident to a non-resident, and FEMA sets the rules on price, timing and reporting.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 7 November 2026·5 min read

Plan the buyout with us
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- Resident-to-non-resident transfer: price not less than fair value; FC-TRS within 60 days.
- Up to 25% of the price can be deferred within 18 months; stamp duty 0.015%.
- Check licences, related-party deals, guarantees and change-of-control clauses first.

Planning a buyout? We value the shares, run the diligence on the JV and file FC-TRS, from India.Free 15-min callDue diligence

## The FEMA rules on the purchase

Point | Rule | 

Is it allowed? | Yes, if the sector allows the higher foreign stake under the automatic route; otherwise government approval is needed. Buyers from countries sharing a land border with India need approval (Press Note 3) | 

Price | Not less than fair value for unlisted shares, under an internationally accepted pricing method, certified by a CA, a SEBI-registered merchant banker or a practising cost accountant | 

Deferred payment | Up to 25% of the price can be paid within 18 months; escrow and indemnity holdbacks on the same terms | 

Reporting | Form FC-TRS within 60 days of the payment or the transfer, whichever is earlier, through the AD bank on the FIRMS portal | 

Stamp duty | 0.015% of the consideration on the share transfer | 

## Tax on both sides

- The Indian partner pays capital gains tax on the sale.

- You, the buyer: if you buy below fair market value, the shortfall can be taxed in India as your income. The FEMA floor and the tax valuation should line up, so one valuation report should address both.

- Check whether any part of the price is really for a non-compete or brand: it may be taxed differently and needs separate drafting.

## Diligence before you buy the rest

You may have sat on the board for years, but the Indian partner usually ran operations. Before paying for control, check:

- Licences and assets in the partner’s name: land, leases, trademarks, government licences, bank guarantees.

- Related-party dealings: supplies, rent, services or loans between the JV and the partner’s group, and whether they continue after exit.

- Guarantees the partner gave for JV loans, which lenders will want replaced.

- Change-of-control clauses in customer contracts, loans and leases.

- Employees and key managers who are loyal to the partner.

- Tax and FEMA history: pending notices, transfer pricing, and whether past foreign investment filings (FC-GPR, FC-TRS, annual FLA return) were made on time.

- Competition approval: large deals can need CCI clearance under the deal-value threshold.

## Typical sequence

- Check the sector cap, route and any approvals.

- Run focused diligence and agree the price with an independent valuation.

- Sign the share purchase agreement, with escrow or deferred payment if needed.

- Pay through banking channels; the AD bank records it.

- Transfer the shares (demat), pay stamp duty and file FC-TRS within 60 days.

- Update the board, the registers and the MCA filings; replace the partner’s guarantees.

Related: setting up a joint venture in India, acquiring a company in India, FC-TRS filing guide and due diligence on Indian partners.

## Sources

- RBI: Master Direction, Foreign Investment in India
- Aviva: agreement to purchase the remaining 26% stake in its India joint venture

## Frequently asked questions
Can a foreign company buy out its Indian joint venture partner?
Yes, if the sector allows the higher foreign stake under the automatic route, or with government approval where needed. The purchase is a share transfer from a resident to a non-resident under FEMA.

What is the minimum price when a foreign partner buys shares from an Indian partner?
For unlisted shares, not less than fair value under an internationally accepted pricing method, certified by a chartered accountant, a SEBI-registered merchant banker or a practising cost accountant.

Which form is filed when a non-resident buys shares from a resident?
Form FC-TRS, filed through the AD bank on the RBI FIRMS portal within 60 days of the payment or the transfer, whichever is earlier.

Can part of the price be deferred in an Indian share purchase?
Yes. Up to 25% of the total consideration can be paid within 18 months, and escrow or indemnity holdbacks are allowed on the same terms.

NRI · Gifts

# Parents in India sending you money abroad: limits, TCS and tax both sides

Helping with a house deposit in Toronto, a car in London or a cushion in New Jersey? Parents in India can send a gift abroad legally and without tax for either side in most cases. The details that trip people up are TCS and the reporting in your country.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 7 November 2026·5 min read

Plan the gift properly
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- LRS: US$250,000 per parent per year; TCS of 20% above ₹10 lakh, refundable.
- No Indian tax for parent or child on the gift.
- No tax on receipt in the US, UK, Canada or Australia; US Form 3520 above US$100,000.

Planning a large gift? We work out the TCS, the paperwork and the reporting in your country before the money moves.WhatsApp usFree 15-min callTransfer checker

## The India side

Point | Rule | 

How it is sent | Under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS), from the parent’s own bank account | 

Limit | US$250,000 per parent per financial year, so up to US$500,000 from both parents | 

TCS | 20% on the amount above ₹10 lakh a year, collected by the bank. It is not a cost: the parent claims it against their tax or as a refund | 

Indian tax for you | None. Gifts from relatives, including parents, are exempt | 

Indian tax for your parents | None on the gift itself. Income you later earn on it is yours | 

Another route: your parents can gift rupees into your NRO account. That is still within their LRS limit, and getting it abroad from NRO needs Forms 145 and 146.

## Your country’s side

Where you live | Tax on the gift | What to watch | 

United States | None | Form 3520 if gifts from foreign persons exceed US$100,000 in the year | 

United Kingdom | None | Keep the gift letter; your bank will ask about the source of funds | 

Canada | None | Lenders want a gift letter for a house deposit; T1135 if you then hold foreign property over CAD 100,000 | 

Australia | None | Keep evidence that it is a gift, not income or a loan | 

Europe | Possibly | Germany, France, Spain, Ireland and the Netherlands can tax gifts received by residents | 

## Paperwork that makes it smooth

- A short gift letter from each parent: amount, relationship, “no repayment expected”.

- Parents’ PAN and their bank’s LRS form (A2) and declaration.

- Proof the money is theirs: bank statement, FD maturity or sale deed.

- Your account details abroad, in your name.

## Common mistakes

- Sending from a relative’s account but calling it the parent’s gift.

- Forgetting that the TCS is refundable, and losing it by not claiming it in the parent’s return.

- In the US, missing Form 3520 because “there was no tax”.

Related: TCS on foreign remittances, the TCS calculator and the transfer checker.

## Sources

- RBI: FAQs on the Liberalised Remittance Scheme
- IRS: About Form 3520
- GOV.UK: Tax on foreign income

## Frequently asked questions
How much money can parents in India send to their child abroad?
Up to US$250,000 per parent per financial year under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme, so up to US$500,000 from both parents.

Is TCS charged when parents send a gift abroad?
Yes. TCS of 20% applies to the amount above ₹10 lakh in a financial year. The parent can claim it against their income tax or as a refund.

Is a gift from parents in India taxable for an NRI child?
Not in India: gifts from relatives are exempt. In the US, UK, Canada and Australia there is no tax on a gift received, though the US requires Form 3520 above US$100,000 a year.

Do I need a gift letter?
It is strongly advised. Banks abroad and lenders ask for one, and it shows the money is a gift and not income or a loan.

Please note: this guide is general information based on the rules as they stood on the review date above. Regulations and RBI/CBDT procedures change often — please get advice on your specific facts before acting.

NRI · Inheritance

# Inherited money in India? How to get it to your account abroad

Losing a parent is hard enough. The paperwork to move what they left you from India is the last thing you want to fight with from another country. India has no inheritance tax, and the money can come out. Here is the order to do it in.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 7 November 2026·5 min read

Get your inheritance moved
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- No inheritance tax in India; later income and gains are the heir's.
- Send up to US$1 million a year with Forms 145 and 146 and the inheritance papers.
- US: Form 3520 over US$100,000; UK, Canada, Australia: no tax on receipt.

Dealing with this from abroad? We coordinate the claims, the tax and the transfer, and keep your trips to India to a minimum.WhatsApp usFree 15-min callTransfer checker

## Step by step

- Gather the documents: death certificate, the will (with probate where required) or a succession or legal heir certificate, your PAN, passport and proof of relationship.

- Claim each asset as nominee or legal heir:
- Bank deposits: the bank’s claim form; funds go to your NRO account.
- Shares: transmission to your NRI demat account through the depository participant.
- Mutual funds: transmission request with the fund house or registrar.
- Property: mutation in the land records and the society; then sell or keep.

- Settle Indian tax: no tax on the inheritance itself, but income after the date of death (interest, rent) and gains when you sell are yours to report. Property sales attract TDS; a lower TDS certificate (Form 128) avoids excess.

- Send it abroad: up to US$1 million per financial year from NRO balances, sale proceeds and inherited assets, with Form 145, a CA certificate in Form 146 and the inheritance documents. Larger amounts can be spread over years or approved by the RBI.

## What your country expects

Where you live | Tax on the inheritance | Reporting | 

United States | None for you | Form 3520 for bequests from a foreign person over US$100,000; later income and gains are taxable in the US | 

United Kingdom | No UK tax on receiving it | Later Indian income and gains are taxable in the UK | 

Canada | None | T1135 if your foreign property costs over CAD 100,000 | 

Australia | None | Keep the will and claim papers for the ATO; later income and gains are taxable | 

Europe | Possibly | Several countries tax inheritances received by residents | 

## Tips from the field

- Start with the nominations: a nominee claim is much faster than a succession certificate.

- Do the property mutation before you try to sell.

- Keep every claim letter: the bank sending the money abroad will ask for the chain from the death certificate to the money.

Related: repatriation from NRO, TDS on property sale by NRIs and demat and mutual funds for NRIs.

## Sources

- RBI: Master Direction on remittance of assets (USD 1 million limit)
- RBI: FAQs on remittance of assets
- IRS: About Form 3520

## Frequently asked questions
Is there inheritance tax in India?
No. India has no inheritance or estate tax. Income earned on the inherited assets after the date of death, and gains when you sell them, are taxable for the heir.

How much inherited money can an NRI transfer abroad?
Up to US$1 million per financial year, covering NRO balances, sale proceeds and inherited assets together, with Form 145, a CA certificate in Form 146 and the inheritance documents.

Do I pay US tax on an inheritance from India?
No US tax on receiving it, but bequests from foreign persons over US$100,000 in a year must be reported on Form 3520. Later income and gains are taxable in the US.

Can I claim an inheritance in India without travelling?
Often yes. Many claims, transmissions and the transfer can be handled with documents sent from abroad, with signatures attested at the Indian consulate where needed.

Please note: this guide is general information based on the rules as they stood on the review date above. Regulations and RBI/CBDT procedures change often — please get advice on your specific facts before acting.

Property sold, an inheritance, NRO savings, or parents sending you money: we get the tax settled, the CA certificate issued, Form 145 filed and the bank satisfied, so the money reaches your account abroad. Everything is handled remotely.

## Who we help

- NRIs selling property in India: TDS, a lower TDS certificate, capital gains and getting the proceeds out.

- Heirs repatriating an inheritance from parents: bank accounts, deposits, shares and property.

- NRIs with NRO savings: rent, dividends, pension and old resident savings.

- Parents in India sending money to children abroad under LRS, and the TCS on it.

- NRIs sending money home: NRE vs NRO, buying property, investing, gifts to family.

## What we do

- Work out the Indian tax and file returns or claim TDS refunds.

- Apply for a lower TDS certificate (Form 128) before a property sale.

- Issue the CA certificate (Form 146) and file Form 145.

Yes. Documents are shared digitally, forms are filed online, and we coordinate with your bank. Some banks need your signature or a video call, which we schedule.

FAST-DS · NRIs

# FAST-DS for NRIs abroad: do you still need it?

Most NRIs assume an Indian foreign-asset scheme has nothing to do with them. But if you were resident in India in any year while holding something abroad, and it never went into Schedule FA, that year can still come back. FAST-DS closes on 31 December 2026.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 6 November 2026·5 min read

Check your FAST-DS position
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- NRIs today can still need FAST-DS for years they were resident in India.
- Common cases: accounts or RSUs before moving, the year of the move, student accounts.
- Flat ₹1 lakh for taxed-income assets; file online from abroad by 31 December 2026.

Not sure if it applies? Send us your India and abroad timeline; we tell you in one reply.WhatsApp usFree 15-min callHow we file

## When an NRI needs to look at FAST-DS

Your story | Why it matters | 

You opened a UK, US, Canadian or Australian account or got RSUs before you moved, while still resident in India | Each resident year needed Schedule FA | 

Your year of moving was still a resident year in India | The new foreign salary account and any foreign income belonged in that year’s return | 

You studied abroad, came back to work in India, then left again | The account from your student days may have been open during your Indian working years | 

You plan to return to India | Once resident again, everything abroad must be reported; clear the past first. See returning NRIs | 

You have been non-resident in every year you held the asset | No Schedule FA was needed. FAST-DS is not for you | 

The scheme is open to people who are non-resident today, if they were resident in India in the year the foreign asset was acquired or the foreign income arose.

## What it costs

- Asset bought from income already taxed in India, or while you were a non-resident, and only missing from Schedule FA: a flat ₹1 lakh (assets up to ₹5 crore).

- Foreign income that should have been taxed in India but was not: 30% tax plus an equal amount (up to ₹1 crore).

- Small holdings: since 1 October 2024 the ₹10 lakh penalty is not applied where foreign assets other than property total ₹20 lakh or less. Check before paying.

Work it out with the free FAST-DS calculator.

## Filing from abroad

- Everything is online: Form 1 on the e-filing portal, payment online, Form 3 after paying.

- You need your Indian PAN login and Aadhaar OTP or a digital signature for verification.

- Foreign bank statements from the year you opened the account are the slow part: bank accounts are valued at the total deposits since opening. Ask for them now.

## Got the department’s email?

Many NRIs received the “overseas financial interests” email too. It is an advisory, not a notice. See what the FAST-DS email means.

## Sources

- Income Tax Department: FAST-DS FAQs
- TaxGuru: Received an email on FAST-DS 2026?

## Frequently asked questions
Can an NRI file FAST-DS?
Yes, if you were resident in India in the year the foreign asset was acquired or the foreign income arose, even if you are non-resident today.

I have always been an NRI while holding my foreign accounts. Do I need FAST-DS?
No. Schedule FA applies only to residents, so assets held only in non-resident years did not need reporting in India.

Can I file FAST-DS from the UK, US, Canada or Australia?
Yes. Form 1 is filed on the e-filing portal, payment is online, and verification is by Aadhaar OTP or a digital signature.

What is the deadline for FAST-DS?
Form 1 must be filed by 31 December 2026. Payment follows once the department issues Form 2.

Please note: this guide is general information based on the rules as they stood on the review date above. Regulations and RBI/CBDT procedures change often — please get advice on your specific facts before acting.

NRIs in the UK · Money transfers

# Money between India and the UK: limits, forms and UK tax

Sold a flat in Pune, inherited from your parents, or just want your NRO savings in your UK account? Here is what India allows, the paperwork your bank will ask for, and what HMRC expects since the non-dom rules ended.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 6 November 2026·6 min read

Get your transfer done right
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- NRO to UK: up to USD 1 million a year after Indian tax, with Forms 145 and 146.
- No UK tax on a gift from parents; Indian interest, rent and gains are taxable in the UK since April 2025.
- Keep source-of-funds papers ready for your UK bank.

Moving a large amount? We prepare Form 145 and the CA certificate, handle TDS on property sales and talk to your bank.WhatsApp usFree 15-min callTransfer checker

## India to UK: what can go, and how
Money in India | Can it go abroad? | Limit and paperwork | 

NRE or FCNR deposit | Yes, freely | No limit. No Indian tax on NRE interest | 

NRO balance: rent, dividends, pension, savings from before you left | Yes, after Indian tax | Up to USD 1 million per financial year, with Form 145 and usually a CA certificate in Form 146 | 

Sale of a flat or land | Yes, after TDS and tax | Within the USD 1 million. Proceeds of up to two homes bought with foreign money or NRE funds can go back up to the amount you paid. A lower TDS certificate (Form 128) stops excess TDS | 

Inheritance from parents | Yes | Within the USD 1 million, with the will or succession papers. India has no inheritance tax | 

Gift from your parents in India | Yes, they send it under LRS | Up to USD 250,000 per parent per year. TCS of 20% above ₹10 lakh, which they can adjust against their tax | 

## UK to India: where to send it
Send it to | Best for | Indian tax | 

NRE account | Savings you may want to take back later | Interest tax-free in India (but taxable where you live) | 

NRO account | Paying Indian bills, EMIs, joint use with Indian income | Interest taxable in India, TDS deducted | 

Your parents’ account | Supporting family | Gifts to relatives are not taxed in India | 

Property, mutual funds, shares | Investing in India through NRE or NRO | Gains taxed in India; NRIs cannot buy farm land | 

## What the UK taxes and checks

- Worldwide income: since 6 April 2025 the remittance basis has gone. UK residents are taxed on Indian interest (including NRE interest), rent and gains as they arise, with credit for Indian tax under the India-UK treaty. People arriving after 10 years outside the UK can claim the 4-year foreign income and gains relief.

- Gifts and inheritances from India: receiving money from your parents is not income in the UK, so there is no UK income tax on it. Keep the gift letter and their bank trail.

- Property sale in India: the gain is taxable in the UK too if you are UK resident, with credit for the Indian tax paid.

- Your UK bank will ask for the source of funds on a large receipt. Form 145, the CA certificate, the sale deed or will are what satisfy them.
FAST-DS check before 31 December 2026: if you were resident in India in any year while holding a foreign account, shares or RSUs, and they were not in Schedule FA, see FAST-DS for NRIs abroad.

## Steps to send money from India

- Pay or settle Indian tax on the money (TDS on rent, interest or property sale).
- Move it to your NRO account if it is not there already.
- Get the CA certificate (Form 146) and file Form 145 online.
- Give your bank the forms, the source documents and its remittance request. It sends the money to your account abroad.
Related: repatriating money from an NRO account, NRE vs NRO vs FCNR, TDS on property sale by NRIs and the free transfer checker.

## Sources

- RBI: Master Direction on remittance of assets (USD 1 million limit)
- RBI: FAQs on remittance of assets
- GOV.UK: Tax on foreign income
Parents sending you money? Gift from parents in India: limits and tax.
Inherited assets in India? How to transfer an inheritance abroad.

## Frequently asked questions
How much money can an NRI in the UK transfer from India?
From an NRO account, up to USD 1 million per financial year, covering balances, property sale proceeds and inheritance, after Indian tax. NRE and FCNR balances can be sent without limit.

Is money received from India taxable in the UK?
A gift or inheritance from your parents is not income, so no UK income tax. But income from India, such as interest, rent and gains, is taxable in the UK for UK residents since April 2025, with credit for Indian tax.

Is NRE interest taxable in the UK?
Yes, for UK residents. It is tax-free only in India. Claim the foreign income relief if you qualify as a recent arrival.

Which forms are needed to send money from India to the UK?
Form 145 (the old 15CA) filed online, and usually a chartered accountant's certificate in Form 146 (the old 15CB), plus the source documents your bank asks for.

# Money between India and the US: limits, forms and IRS reporting

Parents sending you money, an inheritance, or selling property in India and moving it to your US account? India’s limits are the easy part. The IRS forms are where people get penalised.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 6 November 2026·6 min read

Get your transfer done right
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- NRO to US: up to USD 1 million a year after Indian tax, with Forms 145 and 146.
- Gifts or inheritances from India over US$100,000 a year: Form 3520.
- FBAR for Indian accounts over US$10,000; Indian mutual funds are PFICs.

Moving a large amount? We prepare Form 145 and the CA certificate, handle TDS on property sales and talk to your bank.WhatsApp usFree 15-min callTransfer checker

## India to USA: what can go, and how
Money in India | Can it go abroad? | Limit and paperwork | 

NRE or FCNR deposit | Yes, freely | No limit. No Indian tax on NRE interest | 

NRO balance: rent, dividends, pension, savings from before you left | Yes, after Indian tax | Up to USD 1 million per financial year, with Form 145 and usually a CA certificate in Form 146 | 

Sale of a flat or land | Yes, after TDS and tax | Within the USD 1 million. Proceeds of up to two homes bought with foreign money or NRE funds can go back up to the amount you paid. A lower TDS certificate (Form 128) stops excess TDS | 

Inheritance from parents | Yes | Within the USD 1 million, with the will or succession papers. India has no inheritance tax | 

Gift from your parents in India | Yes, they send it under LRS | Up to USD 250,000 per parent per year. TCS of 20% above ₹10 lakh, which they can adjust against their tax | 

## USA to India: where to send it
Send it to | Best for | Indian tax | 

NRE account | Savings you may want to take back later | Interest tax-free in India (but taxable where you live) | 

NRO account | Paying Indian bills, EMIs, joint use with Indian income | Interest taxable in India, TDS deducted | 

Your parents’ account | Supporting family | Gifts to relatives are not taxed in India | 

Property, mutual funds, shares | Investing in India through NRE or NRO | Gains taxed in India; NRIs cannot buy farm land | 

## What the US taxes and reports
Situation | US requirement | 

Gift or inheritance from parents in India over US$100,000 in a year | Form 3520. No tax, but heavy penalties if not filed | 

Indian bank accounts (NRE, NRO, FD) above US$10,000 in total at any time | FBAR (FinCEN 114), and Form 8938 above the FATCA thresholds | 

Indian mutual funds | Treated as PFICs: punitive tax and Form 8621. Get advice before buying more | 

NRE interest, Indian rent, property gains | Taxable in the US, with foreign tax credit for Indian tax | 

You send a gift to your parents above the annual exclusion | You file Form 709; tax is rarely due because of the lifetime exemption | 

Cash or money-order transfers to India | 1% remittance tax since 2026; bank transfers and US cards are exempt. See the 1% remittance tax | 

FAST-DS check before 31 December 2026: if you were resident in India in any year while holding a foreign account, shares or RSUs, and they were not in Schedule FA, see FAST-DS for NRIs abroad.

## Steps to send money from India

- Pay or settle Indian tax on the money (TDS on rent, interest or property sale).
- Move it to your NRO account if it is not there already.
- Get the CA certificate (Form 146) and file Form 145 online.
- Give your bank the forms, the source documents and its remittance request. It sends the money to your account abroad.
Related: repatriating money from an NRO account, NRE vs NRO vs FCNR, TDS on property sale by NRIs and the free transfer checker.

## Sources

- IRS: About Form 3520
- IRS: Report of Foreign Bank and Financial Accounts (FBAR)
- IRS: Comparison of Form 8938 and FBAR requirements
Parents sending you money? Gift from parents in India: limits and tax.
Inherited assets in India? How to transfer an inheritance abroad.

## Frequently asked questions
Do I pay US tax on money my parents send from India?
No. A gift is not income. But if gifts from foreign persons exceed US$100,000 in a year, you must report them on Form 3520.

How much can an NRI in the US repatriate from India?
Up to USD 1 million per financial year from NRO balances, property sale proceeds and inheritance, after Indian tax, with Forms 145 and 146. NRE and FCNR balances have no limit.

Do I need to report Indian bank accounts to the IRS?
Yes. If your foreign accounts exceed US$10,000 in total at any point in the year, file an FBAR; Form 8938 may also apply above the FATCA thresholds.

Are Indian mutual funds a problem for US residents?
Yes. They are generally PFICs for US tax, with punitive tax and Form 8621 reporting. Review them before investing more.

NRIs in Canada · Money transfers

# Money between India and Canada: limits, forms and CRA rules

Bringing your Indian savings to Canada, receiving help from your parents, or selling property back home? Here is what India allows and what the CRA expects you to report.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 6 November 2026·6 min read

Get your transfer done right
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- NRO to Canada: up to USD 1 million a year after Indian tax, with Forms 145 and 146.
- No Canadian tax on gifts or inheritances; T1135 above CAD 100,000 of foreign property.
- NRE interest and Indian rent are taxable in Canada.

Moving a large amount? We prepare Form 145 and the CA certificate, handle TDS on property sales and talk to your bank.WhatsApp usFree 15-min callTransfer checker

## India to Canada: what can go, and how
Money in India | Can it go abroad? | Limit and paperwork | 

NRE or FCNR deposit | Yes, freely | No limit. No Indian tax on NRE interest | 

NRO balance: rent, dividends, pension, savings from before you left | Yes, after Indian tax | Up to USD 1 million per financial year, with Form 145 and usually a CA certificate in Form 146 | 

Sale of a flat or land | Yes, after TDS and tax | Within the USD 1 million. Proceeds of up to two homes bought with foreign money or NRE funds can go back up to the amount you paid. A lower TDS certificate (Form 128) stops excess TDS | 

Inheritance from parents | Yes | Within the USD 1 million, with the will or succession papers. India has no inheritance tax | 

Gift from your parents in India | Yes, they send it under LRS | Up to USD 250,000 per parent per year. TCS of 20% above ₹10 lakh, which they can adjust against their tax | 

## Canada to India: where to send it
Send it to | Best for | Indian tax | 

NRE account | Savings you may want to take back later | Interest tax-free in India (but taxable where you live) | 

NRO account | Paying Indian bills, EMIs, joint use with Indian income | Interest taxable in India, TDS deducted | 

Your parents’ account | Supporting family | Gifts to relatives are not taxed in India | 

Property, mutual funds, shares | Investing in India through NRE or NRO | Gains taxed in India; NRIs cannot buy farm land | 

## What Canada taxes and reports

- Gifts and inheritances: Canada has no tax on money you receive as a gift or inheritance from India.

- Form T1135: if the cost of your foreign property (Indian bank deposits, shares, mutual funds, a rented flat) is over CAD 100,000 at any time in the year, you must file it. Your own home in India used personally is excluded.

- Worldwide income: NRE interest, Indian rent and gains on Indian property are taxable in Canada for residents, with foreign tax credit for Indian tax.

- Banks report international transfers of CAD 10,000 or more to FINTRAC. That is routine; just keep the paper trail.
FAST-DS check before 31 December 2026: if you were resident in India in any year while holding a foreign account, shares or RSUs, and they were not in Schedule FA, see FAST-DS for NRIs abroad.

## Steps to send money from India

- Pay or settle Indian tax on the money (TDS on rent, interest or property sale).
- Move it to your NRO account if it is not there already.
- Get the CA certificate (Form 146) and file Form 145 online.
- Give your bank the forms, the source documents and its remittance request. It sends the money to your account abroad.
Related: repatriating money from an NRO account, NRE vs NRO vs FCNR, TDS on property sale by NRIs and the free transfer checker.

## Sources

- RBI: Master Direction on remittance of assets (USD 1 million limit)
- CRA: Form T1135, Foreign Income Verification Statement
- FINTRAC (Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada)
Parents sending you money? Gift from parents in India: limits and tax.
Inherited assets in India? How to transfer an inheritance abroad.

## Frequently asked questions
Is money from India taxable in Canada?
A gift or inheritance is not taxable in Canada. Income from India, such as NRE interest, rent and capital gains, is taxable for Canadian residents, with credit for Indian tax.

Do I need to file T1135 for Indian accounts?
Yes, if the total cost of your specified foreign property, including Indian deposits and investments, exceeds CAD 100,000 at any time in the year.

How much can I repatriate from India to Canada?
Up to USD 1 million per financial year from NRO balances, property sale proceeds and inheritance, after Indian tax, with Forms 145 and 146.

Is NRE interest taxable in Canada?
Yes, for Canadian residents. It is tax-free only in India.

NRIs in Australia · Money transfers

# Money between India and Australia: limits, forms and ATO rules

Selling the family flat, receiving an inheritance, or moving your NRO savings to Australia? India’s rules decide how much can go; the ATO decides what is taxable once it lands.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 6 November 2026·6 min read

Get your transfer done right
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- NRO to Australia: up to USD 1 million a year after Indian tax, with Forms 145 and 146.
- No gift or inheritance tax in Australia; keep documents for large deposits.
- Indian interest, rent and gains go in your Australian return with an offset.

Moving a large amount? We prepare Form 145 and the CA certificate, handle TDS on property sales and talk to your bank.WhatsApp usFree 15-min callTransfer checker

## India to Australia: what can go, and how
Money in India | Can it go abroad? | Limit and paperwork | 

NRE or FCNR deposit | Yes, freely | No limit. No Indian tax on NRE interest | 

NRO balance: rent, dividends, pension, savings from before you left | Yes, after Indian tax | Up to USD 1 million per financial year, with Form 145 and usually a CA certificate in Form 146 | 

Sale of a flat or land | Yes, after TDS and tax | Within the USD 1 million. Proceeds of up to two homes bought with foreign money or NRE funds can go back up to the amount you paid. A lower TDS certificate (Form 128) stops excess TDS | 

Inheritance from parents | Yes | Within the USD 1 million, with the will or succession papers. India has no inheritance tax | 

Gift from your parents in India | Yes, they send it under LRS | Up to USD 250,000 per parent per year. TCS of 20% above ₹10 lakh, which they can adjust against their tax | 

## Australia to India: where to send it
Send it to | Best for | Indian tax | 

NRE account | Savings you may want to take back later | Interest tax-free in India (but taxable where you live) | 

NRO account | Paying Indian bills, EMIs, joint use with Indian income | Interest taxable in India, TDS deducted | 

Your parents’ account | Supporting family | Gifts to relatives are not taxed in India | 

Property, mutual funds, shares | Investing in India through NRE or NRO | Gains taxed in India; NRIs cannot buy farm land | 

## What Australia taxes and checks

- No gift or inheritance tax: money your parents give you, or leave you, is not taxed in Australia. Keep the gift letter or will, because the ATO can ask where a large deposit came from.

- Worldwide income: Australian residents are taxed on NRE interest, Indian rent and Indian capital gains, with a foreign income tax offset for Indian tax.

- Indian property sale: the gain is in your Australian return too. The Indian TDS and tax become your offset.

- Banks report international transfers to AUSTRAC. That is routine; the papers from India explain the money.
FAST-DS check before 31 December 2026: if you were resident in India in any year while holding a foreign account, shares or RSUs, and they were not in Schedule FA, see FAST-DS for NRIs abroad.

## Steps to send money from India

- Pay or settle Indian tax on the money (TDS on rent, interest or property sale).
- Move it to your NRO account if it is not there already.
- Get the CA certificate (Form 146) and file Form 145 online.
- Give your bank the forms, the source documents and its remittance request. It sends the money to your account abroad.
Related: repatriating money from an NRO account, NRE vs NRO vs FCNR, TDS on property sale by NRIs and the free transfer checker.

## Sources

- RBI: Master Direction on remittance of assets (USD 1 million limit)
- RBI: FAQs on remittance of assets
- Australian Taxation Office
- AUSTRAC
Parents sending you money? Gift from parents in India: limits and tax.
Inherited assets in India? How to transfer an inheritance abroad.

## Frequently asked questions
Is money from India taxable in Australia?
Gifts and inheritances are not taxed in Australia. Income from India, such as interest, rent and capital gains, is taxable for Australian residents, with a foreign income tax offset.

How much can I transfer from India to Australia?
Up to USD 1 million per financial year from NRO balances, property sale proceeds and inheritance, after Indian tax, with Forms 145 and 146. NRE balances have no limit.

Do I pay tax in both India and Australia on a property sale?
India taxes the gain first through TDS and your Indian return. Australia also taxes it if you are resident, but gives an offset for the Indian tax.

Is NRE interest taxable in Australia?
Yes, for Australian residents. It is tax-free only in India.

# Money between India and Europe: limits, forms and gift tax

Working in Germany, the Netherlands, Ireland or France and moving money to or from India? India’s side is the same everywhere in Europe. The surprise is that some European countries tax gifts and inheritances you receive.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 6 November 2026·6 min read

Get your transfer done right
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- NRO to Europe: up to USD 1 million a year after Indian tax, with Forms 145 and 146.
- Several European countries tax gifts and inheritances received; check before a large gift.
- Indian income is usually taxable locally, with treaty credit.

Moving a large amount? We prepare Form 145 and the CA certificate, handle TDS on property sales and talk to your bank.WhatsApp usFree 15-min callTransfer checker

## India to Europe: what can go, and how
Money in India | Can it go abroad? | Limit and paperwork | 

NRE or FCNR deposit | Yes, freely | No limit. No Indian tax on NRE interest | 

NRO balance: rent, dividends, pension, savings from before you left | Yes, after Indian tax | Up to USD 1 million per financial year, with Form 145 and usually a CA certificate in Form 146 | 

Sale of a flat or land | Yes, after TDS and tax | Within the USD 1 million. Proceeds of up to two homes bought with foreign money or NRE funds can go back up to the amount you paid. A lower TDS certificate (Form 128) stops excess TDS |

Property, mutual funds, shares | Investing in India through NRE or NRO | Gains taxed in India; NRIs cannot buy farm land | 

## What European countries tax

- Gift and inheritance tax on the receiver: unlike the UK, US, Canada and Australia, countries such as Germany, France, Spain, Ireland and the Netherlands can tax a gift or inheritance received by their residents, with allowances that depend on the relationship. Check before your parents send a large amount.

- Worldwide income: residents are generally taxed on Indian interest (including NRE), rent and gains, with credit under India’s tax treaty with that country.

- Reporting: foreign accounts and assets often have to be declared in your local return.
FAST-DS check before 31 December 2026: if you were resident in India in any year while holding a foreign account, shares or RSUs, and they were not in Schedule FA, see FAST-DS for NRIs abroad.

It can be. Several European countries, including Germany, France, Spain, Ireland and the Netherlands, tax gifts and inheritances received by their residents, with allowances. Check the local rules before a large transfer.

Up to USD 1 million per financial year from NRO balances, property sale proceeds and inheritance, after Indian tax, with Forms 145 and 146. NRE balances have no limit.

FAST-DS · Foreign assets

# Got the FAST-DS email? Here is what it means

Since 25 September 2026, the Income Tax Department has been emailing and texting taxpayers that its records indicate they may have overseas financial interests, and pointing them to FAST-DS. It is not a notice, but it should not be ignored.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 5 November 2026·4 min read

Get your position checked before 31 December
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- The email is an advisory, not a notice; no reply is needed.
- Check AIS > Foreign Assets Information against Schedule FA in each resident-year return.
- Revise FY 2025-26 free by 31 Dec 2026; use FAST-DS (₹1 lakh flat for taxed-income assets) for earlier years.

## What the email is

- It is an advisory, not a legal notice. It does not ask for a reply and sets no date to respond.

- It is based on data that foreign banks, brokers and custodians share with India under CRS and FATCA.

- A real notice appears under Pending Actions on the e-filing portal. Check there too.

- The department now has a record that you were told. If proceedings start later, “I didn’t know” will be harder to argue.

## Where to see what they have

- Log in to the e-filing portal directly. Do not use the link in the email or SMS.

- Open AIS through the Compliance Portal and look for Foreign Assets Information.

- Compare it with Schedule FA and the foreign income schedules in each return you filed as a resident.

The AIS view is not complete. List everything you held abroad yourself: bank accounts, brokerage accounts, RSUs and ESOPs, insurance policies and property.

## Which route fits

Your position | What to do | Last date | 

Everything was reported | Nothing. Keep your returns and statements ready | — | 

Missed only in the FY 2025-26 return | Revised return with Schedule FA | 31 Dec 2026 with no fee (to 31 Mar 2027 with a fee) | 

Missed in earlier years; asset bought from taxed income or while you were an NRI (RSUs, ESOPs, old bank account, US stocks) | FAST-DS: flat ₹1 lakh, for assets up to ₹5 crore | 31 Dec 2026 | 

Foreign income that was taxable in India but never taxed | FAST-DS: 30% tax plus an equal amount, up to ₹1 crore | 31 Dec 2026 | 

Foreign assets other than property of ₹20 lakh or less | The ₹10 lakh penalty is not applied for defaults from 1 October 2024. Check this before paying anything | — | 

Work out your number with the free FAST-DS calculator, and read the full FAST-DS guide.

## Two things people get wrong

- A foreign bank account is valued at the total deposits since you opened it, not the current balance. See FAST-DS for foreign bank accounts.

- Old foreign statements take time. Overseas banks can take weeks to send them, so request them now.

## Who is getting it

Reported cases include employees with RSUs from a foreign employer, people with accounts from their student years abroad, returning NRIs who still hold foreign accounts, and small US share investors. People who report every year have also received it, for example where one year or one brokerage account was left out. See FAST-DS for RSUs and ESOPs and FAST-DS for returning NRIs.

## Sources

- TaxGuru: Received an email on FAST-DS 2026? What it means
- Paasa: Income tax email on foreign assets and FAST-DS
- CAalley (Indian Express): Income Tax Department shares foreign assets info, nudges for disclosure
- Income Tax Department: FAST-DS FAQs

## Frequently asked questions
Is the FAST-DS email from the Income Tax Department a notice?
No. It describes itself as an automated advisory, not a legal notice, and does not ask for a reply. A real notice appears under Pending Actions on the e-filing portal.

Do I need to reply to the income tax email about overseas financial interests?
No reply is required. But check the Foreign Assets Information in your AIS against Schedule FA in your past returns, and correct any gap before 31 December 2026.

Where can I see the foreign asset data the department has?
Log in to the e-filing portal, open AIS through the Compliance Portal and look for Foreign Assets Information. It comes from data shared by foreign institutions under CRS and FATCA, and may not be complete.

I reported everything. Can I ignore the email?
Yes, if every return filed while you were resident shows your foreign assets and income correctly. Keep the returns and foreign statements ready in case questions come later.

What if I only missed it in last year's return?
File a revised return for FY 2025-26 with Schedule FA. There is no fee until 31 December 2026.

Please note: this guide is general information based on the rules as they stood on the review date above. Regulations and RBI/CBDT procedures change often — please get advice on your specific facts before acting.

NRI · Investments

# Demat and mutual funds after becoming an NRI: step by step

You do not need to sell your Indian shares or mutual funds when you move abroad. But a resident demat account cannot simply carry on, and every mutual fund folio needs your new status, address and bank. Here is the order to do it in.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 5 November 2026·5 min read

Get your NRI conversion done
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- Move resident demat holdings to an NRO non-PIS demat by off-market transfer; no need to sell.
- Use NRE PIS for fresh repatriable investment; no intraday or short selling for NRIs.
- Update every mutual fund folio and SIP mandate separately; TDS applies to NRI gains and dividends.

## When does this need to be done?

Under FEMA, you become a non-resident as soon as you leave India for a job or to live abroad, not at the end of the tax year. Your broker, depository participant and fund houses should be told promptly. Holding shares in a resident account after your status has changed is a compliance gap, and brokers can take a week or more to process the paperwork.

## Shares: resident demat to NRI demat

Account | Linked bank | Use it for | 

NRO non-PIS demat and trading | NRO account | Shares you already hold from your resident days. Sale proceeds are non-repatriable, but can be sent abroad within the NRO limits with Form 15CA/15CB | 

NRE PIS demat and trading | NRE account | Fresh investment from your foreign income, on a repatriable basis | 

- Open an NRO (and, if you want, an NRE) bank account, or redesignate your savings account as NRO.

- Open an NRO non-PIS demat and trading account with your broker.

- Move your holdings from the resident demat by an off-market transfer (delivery instruction slip). You do not have to sell them.

- Close the resident demat. Some depository participants now allow the status to be changed on the same account; ask yours.

- Update apps built on your broker (for example smallcase) once the new account is live.

As an NRI, you cannot do intraday trading or short selling in Indian equities, so check any standing strategies.

## Mutual funds and SIPs

- Folios do not move with the demat. Update each fund house or its registrar (CAMS or KFintech) with your NRI status, overseas address, FATCA declaration and an NRE or NRO bank mandate. Units held through a broker’s platform may need a separate transfer request.

- SIPs can usually continue once the mandate is moved to an NRE or NRO account. Money invested from your resident savings stays non-repatriable.

- Some fund houses do not accept investments from residents of the US or Canada. Residents of the UAE, Singapore and the UK can generally invest. Check each fund house.

## Tax and TDS as an NRI

Income | What changes | 

Capital gains on shares and equity funds | Still taxable in India. The broker or fund house deducts TDS on the gain at the time of sale or redemption | 

Dividends | TDS at 20%, or the lower treaty rate if you give a Tax Residency Certificate and Form 10F | 

Refund of excess TDS | Only by filing an Indian return; see ITR for NRIs | 

## Checklist

- Bank: redesignate to NRO, and open an NRE account if you will invest from abroad.

- Broker: NRO non-PIS account, off-market transfer, close the resident demat.

- Mutual funds: status, address, FATCA and bank mandate for every folio.

- NPS and EPF: update status and bank details.

- Tax: Tax Residency Certificate and Form 10F for treaty rates, and a plan for TDS refunds.

Related: moved to Dubai: NRI checklist, US stocks after becoming an NRI and repatriation from an NRO account.

## Sources

- HDFC Bank: What happens to your demat account after a residency change
- Groww: Converting a resident demat account to an NRI demat account
- ICICI Direct: Resident to NRI conversion
- Business Standard: Moving abroad? Changes to make in bank, demat and MF accounts

## Frequently asked questions
Can I keep my Indian shares after becoming an NRI?
Yes. You do not need to sell. Move them from your resident demat to an NRO non-PIS demat account by an off-market transfer, then close the resident demat or ask your depository participant to change its status.

What is the difference between NRE PIS and NRO non-PIS?
An NRO non-PIS account holds shares bought while you were resident, and proceeds go to your NRO account. An NRE PIS account is for fresh investment from foreign income on a repatriable basis.

Can I continue my mutual fund SIPs as an NRI?
Usually yes. Update each folio with your NRI status, overseas address and FATCA details, and move the SIP mandate to an NRE or NRO account. Some fund houses do not accept residents of the US or Canada.

Is TDS deducted on mutual fund redemption for NRIs?
Yes. Fund houses deduct TDS on the capital gain when an NRI redeems units. Excess TDS can be claimed back only by filing an Indian income-tax return.

Please note: this guide is general information based on the rules as they stood on the review date above. Regulations and RBI/CBDT procedures change often — please get advice on your specific facts before acting.

NRI · Foreign shares

# US stocks after becoming an NRI: what changes and what to fix

Many Indians build a US stock portfolio through an app under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme, then move to Dubai, Singapore, the UK or the US for work. The shares can stay, but the tax position, the reporting and the US paperwork all change, and gaps from the years you were resident in India need fixing.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 5 November 2026·6 min read

Get your US holdings reviewed
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- You can keep US shares bought while resident; NRIs are not taxed in India on them.
- Every resident-year return should show them in Schedule FA; FY 2025-26 can be revised free until 31 December 2026.
- File a new W-8BEN within 30 days of moving; Dubai residents face 30% US dividend withholding.

Before 31 December 2026: if your US shares were left out of Schedule FA in your FY 2025-26 return, a revised return filed by 31 December 2026 carries no fee. For earlier years, check whether FAST-DS applies; its last date is also 31 December 2026.

## Can I keep US shares bought while I was resident in India?

Yes. Under FEMA, a person resident outside India may continue to hold foreign assets acquired while resident in India. You do not need to sell. Update your status and address with the investing platform and its US broker, because some platforms limit service to residents of certain countries.

Once you are a non-resident under FEMA, the Liberalised Remittance Scheme no longer governs fresh investment. You can invest from your foreign salary directly, and no Indian TCS applies to money that never leaves an Indian bank.

## How the shares are taxed in India

Your status for the year | US dividends and gains | Schedule FA | 

Resident and ordinarily resident | Taxable in India. Gains after 24 months: 12.5%. Earlier: slab rates. Credit for US tax withheld (Form 67) | Required | 

Resident but not ordinarily resident (RNOR) | Generally not taxable in India | Not required | 

Non-resident | Not taxable in India | Not required | 

US shares are not listed on an Indian stock exchange, so Indian tax treats them like unlisted shares: long-term after 24 months. Your status is decided for each financial year as a whole, so the year you move is often still a resident year. See residential status and RNOR.

## Schedule FA for the years you were resident

- Every return filed as a resident should list the US shares, the brokerage account and the dividends in Schedule FA, even if you sold nothing.

- Schedule FA follows the calendar year. The FY 2025-26 return (AY 2026-27) covers holdings from 1 January to 31 December 2025.

- Omitting it can attract a ₹10 lakh penalty per year under the Black Money Act. Since 1 October 2024, this is not applied where your foreign assets other than property total ₹20 lakh or less. Above that, the relief is lost.

## How to fix a missed disclosure

Year | Route | Last date | 

FY 2025-26 (AY 2026-27) | Revised return with Schedule FA | 31 December 2026 with no fee; up to 31 March 2027 with a fee of ₹1,000 or ₹5,000 | 

Earlier years | Check eligibility for FAST-DS (shares bought from taxed income: flat ₹1 lakh) | 31 December 2026 | 

Unreported dividends or gains | Updated return (ITR-U) with additional tax | Depends on the year; see ITR-U time limits | 

## Update your W-8BEN with the US broker

Your W-8BEN tells the US broker which country you are tax resident in. If that changes, you must give a new form within 30 days. This changes the US tax withheld on dividends:

- As an Indian resident, the India-US tax treaty limits dividend withholding to 25%.

- The US has no income tax treaty with the UAE, so a Dubai resident generally suffers the full 30%.

- Residents of the UK, Singapore, Canada and others get their own treaty rate.

## US estate tax: often missed

For people who are not US citizens or residents, US shares are US assets for US estate tax. The exemption is only US$60,000, whatever country you live in. On a large US portfolio, plan for this, and keep nominee details current with the platform.

## Checklist when you move abroad

- Confirm your residential status for the year of the move and the next year.

- Check Schedule FA in every return filed as a resident while you held the shares.

- Update the platform and the US broker: country of residence, address and a new W-8BEN.

- Keep statements of cost and dates for every lot, for the gain computation if you return.

- Plan for US estate tax if the portfolio is large.

Related: investing in US stocks from India, moved to Dubai: NRI checklist and FAST-DS for returning NRIs.

## Sources

- IRS: About Form W-8BEN
- IRS: United States income tax treaties, A to Z
- IRS: Some nonresidents with US assets must file estate tax returns
- Income Tax Department: FAST-DS FAQs
- Legal500 (S&A Law Offices): Union Budget 2026-27, direct tax
Shares and mutual funds in India? Demat and mutual funds after becoming an NRI.

## Frequently asked questions
Can an NRI keep US stocks bought while resident in India?
Yes. Under FEMA, a person resident outside India can continue to hold foreign assets acquired while resident in India. You do not need to sell them, but update your status with the platform and the US broker.

Is an NRI taxed in India on US stock gains and dividends?
No. A non-resident is not taxed in India on income that arises outside India, such as dividends and gains on US shares. In years you were a resident and ordinarily resident, they are taxable in India, with credit for US tax withheld.

Do NRIs need to fill Schedule FA?
No. Schedule FA applies only to residents who are ordinarily resident. But every return you filed as a resident should show your US shares, and a missed disclosure for FY 2025-26 can be corrected by a revised return, with no fee up to 31 December 2026.

What US tax is withheld on dividends after moving to Dubai?
Generally 30%. The US has no income tax treaty with the UAE, so the 25% rate available to Indian residents under the India-US treaty no longer applies once you update your W-8BEN to the UAE.

Do I need a new W-8BEN after moving abroad?
Yes. If your country of tax residence changes, give your US broker a new W-8BEN within 30 days of the change.

Please note: this guide is general information based on the rules as they stood on the review date above. Regulations and RBI/CBDT procedures change often — please get advice on your specific facts before acting.

Supplier checks · Medical devices

# Buying medical devices from India: check the licence first

India is a growing source of medical devices and consumables. Before you place an order, sign a distribution deal or invest, confirm that your Indian partner actually holds the licence for the device it is selling you. Here is what to ask for and how to read it.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 4 November 2026·5 min read

Get your supplier verified
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- Class A/B manufacturer: Form MD-5 (state authority). Class C/D: Form MD-9 (CDSCO, after site audit).
- Importers need MD-15; sellers and distributors need MD-42 registration.
- Match entity, factory address, device and class to the licence; an Indian licence is not FDA or CE.

Need it checked on the ground? We verify the licence, the company and the factory, and send you a written report.Free 15-min callSupplier verification

## Risk classes

Under India’s Medical Devices Rules, 2017, devices are classified by risk: Class A (low), Class B (low to moderate), Class C (moderate to high) and Class D (high). The class decides who issues the licence and how closely the factory is examined.

## Which licence your supplier should hold

If the supplier… | Licence | Issued by | 

Manufactures Class A or B devices | Form MD-5 (applied for on MD-3) | State Licensing Authority | 

Manufactures Class C or D devices | Form MD-9 (applied for on MD-7), granted after an audit of the site | Central Licensing Authority (CDSCO) | 

Imports devices into India | Form MD-15 import licence (applied for on MD-14) | Central Licensing Authority (CDSCO) | 

Sells or distributes devices it does not make | Form MD-42 registration | State Licensing Authority | 

## How to verify the licence

- Get a copy of the licence and its annexure listing the devices covered.

- Match the details: the company name and the factory address on the licence must match the entity you are contracting with and the site you are told makes your product. Check the company on the Ministry of Corporate Affairs records and its GST registration.

- Match the device: your exact device, model and class must appear on the licence. A licence for one device does not cover another.

- Confirm it is current with the issuing authority, and that it has not been suspended or cancelled.

- See the factory: for anything other than simple low-risk items, a visit is the only way to confirm the licensed site is where the goods are made.

## Beyond the licence

- Quality system: ISO 13485 certification and recent audit reports.

- Your market’s rules: an Indian licence is not a US FDA clearance or an EU CE mark. Check the approvals your own market needs, and who holds them.

- Export documents: ask what the supplier will provide, for example a free sale certificate and test reports.

- Financial health and ownership: filed accounts, charges, litigation and who really owns the business. See red flags in Indian company accounts.

Related: Indian supplier verification and site visits and due diligence on Indian partners.

## Sources

- CDSCO: Regulatory pathway under the Medical Devices Rules, 2017
- CDSCO: FAQs on medical devices

## Frequently asked questions
Which licence does an Indian medical device manufacturer need?
Under the Medical Devices Rules, 2017, manufacturers of Class A and B devices need a licence in Form MD-5 from the State Licensing Authority, and manufacturers of Class C and D devices need a licence in Form MD-9 from the Central Licensing Authority (CDSCO), granted after a site audit.

How do I check an Indian medical device supplier's licence?
Ask for a copy of the licence and its device annexure, match the company name, factory address and your exact device and class against it, confirm with the issuing authority that it is current, and verify the company's registration and the factory itself.

Does an Indian CDSCO licence mean the device can be sold in the US or EU?
No. An Indian licence covers manufacture and sale in India. Selling in the US or EU needs the approvals of those markets, such as US FDA clearance or a CE mark, so check who holds them.

What licence does an Indian importer or distributor of medical devices need?
An importer needs an import licence in Form MD-15 from the Central Licensing Authority, and a business that sells or distributes devices it does not make needs a registration in Form MD-42.

Please note: this guide is general information based on the rules as they stood on the review date above. Regulations and RBI/CBDT procedures change often — please get advice on your specific facts before acting.

# FAST-DS filing, done for you before 31 December

Foreign bank account, RSUs from a US employer, savings from your years abroad, never shown in your Indian return? FAST-DS is a one-time window to put it right at a known cost. We handle the whole filing, from valuation to the final certificate.

Get your FAST-DS filed
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Deadline 31 December 2026. Valuations and bank statements take time. Start now.WhatsApp usFree 15-min callHow we file

## Who we help

- Employees of foreign companies with RSUs, ESPP or ESOP shares at E*Trade, Morgan Stanley, Fidelity, Schwab or similar, never reported in Schedule FA.

- Returning NRIs with bank accounts, pensions or investments from their years abroad.

- Former students with an account left open in the US, UK, Canada or Australia.

- Families with foreign property, insurance or deposits that were never reported.

- Current NRIs who were resident in India when the asset was acquired or the income arose.

## What we do

- Review: list every foreign account, security, RSU, policy and property, and check which ones actually need FAST-DS. Some do not: for example where only the ₹20 lakh Schedule FA threshold matters.

- Classify: decide between Category 1 (60%) and Category 2 (₹1 lakh) for each item, and check the ₹1 crore and ₹5 crore limits.

- Value: compute the value as on 31 March 2026 under the scheme rules, including the sum-of-deposits rule for bank accounts and RBI reference rates.

- File Form 1 on the e-filing portal, with the supporting evidence.

- Check Form 2 (the order of the amount payable), make the payment through challan ITNS 289 with you, and file Form 3 within the deadline.

- Follow through to Form 4 (the payment certificate), and set up correct Schedule FA reporting in your future returns.

## Documents we need

- PAN and e-filing login, and your Indian returns for the years concerned.

- Bank statements for each foreign account from opening to 31 March 2026.

- Brokerage statements and vesting or purchase records for shares, RSUs and ESPP.

- Purchase documents for property and policy documents for insurance or pensions.

- Your travel dates for the relevant years, to confirm residential status.

## Timeline

Step | When | 

Review, valuation and Form 1 | Before 31 December 2026 (no declaration after that date) | 

Form 2 (amount payable) | Issued by the department after you file | 

Payment and Form 3 | Within 2 months from the end of the month Form 2 is received; up to 2 more months with 1% a month interest, after which the declaration is void | 

Form 4 (certificate) | Issued after the payment is verified | 

Fees are fixed upfront after a short review of your holdings. Not sure if you need it? Try the FAST-DS calculator or read the complete FAST-DS guide.

Got the email about “overseas financial interests”? What the FAST-DS email means and what to do.
Living abroad now? FAST-DS for NRIs in the UK, US, Canada and Australia.

## Frequently asked questions
Can you file FAST-DS for me?
Yes. We review your foreign assets, value them as on 31 March 2026, choose the right category, file Form 1, help you pay the amount in Form 2 through challan ITNS 289, file Form 3 and follow through to the Form 4 certificate.

What is the last date for FAST-DS?
31 December 2026. No declaration can be filed after that date, so leave time to collect statements and complete the valuation.

How much does FAST-DS cost?
The scheme amount is 60% of the value for undisclosed assets or income up to ₹1 crore (Category 1), or a flat ₹1 lakh where the asset came from taxed income or was acquired while non-resident and was only missing from Schedule FA, up to ₹5 crore (Category 2). Our professional fee is fixed after a short review.

Do I need FAST-DS if my foreign assets are small?
Not always. Since 1 October 2024 the ₹10 lakh Schedule FA penalty does not apply where foreign assets other than immovable property total ₹20 lakh or less, although you must still report them. We check whether FAST-DS is worth it for you before filing.

Can an NRI file FAST-DS?
Yes, if you were resident in India in the year the foreign asset was acquired or the foreign income arose, even if you are a non-resident today.

## How the calculator works

- Category 1 (undisclosed assets or income, up to ₹1 crore together): 30% tax plus an equal additional amount, 60% in all.

- Category 2 (taxed income or non-resident years, missing only from Schedule FA, up to ₹5 crore): a flat ₹1,00,000.

- Valuation is as on 31 March 2026. For bank accounts, the value is the total of all deposits since the account was opened (deposits made out of withdrawals from the same account are excluded), not the balance. Quoted shares use the higher of cost and the average of the day’s high and low price on 31 March 2026. Foreign currency converts at the RBI reference rate for that date.

- Payment is due within two months from the end of the month you receive Form 2, with up to two more months at 1% a month interest.

Full rules: FAST-DS 2026 guide.

## Frequently asked questions
How is FAST-DS tax calculated?
For undisclosed foreign assets or income up to ₹1 crore in total, tax is 30% of the value plus an additional amount equal to the tax, 60% in all. Where the asset came from taxed income or was acquired while non-resident and was only missing from Schedule FA, up to ₹5 crore, a flat fee of ₹1 lakh applies.

How is a foreign bank account valued under FAST-DS?
At the sum of all deposits made into the account from the date it was opened to 31 March 2026, excluding deposits made out of withdrawals from the same account, converted at the RBI reference rate. It is not the closing balance.

What happens if I don't pay the FAST-DS amount on time?
You must pay within two months from the end of the month in which you receive Form 2. A further two months is allowed with interest at 1% a month; after that the declaration becomes void and is treated as never made.

FAST-DS · Employees of foreign companies

# FAST-DS for RSUs and ESOPs: employees of foreign companies

If you work in India for a US or European company, you probably hold RSUs or ESPP shares in a brokerage account abroad. The tax on vesting is usually deducted through your Indian payroll, but the shares themselves often never make it into Schedule FA. FAST-DS is the cheapest way to fix that.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 4 November 2026·5 min read

Fix your RSU reporting
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Got the email about “overseas financial interests”? What the FAST-DS email means and what to do.
Key takeaways
- RSUs taxed via Indian payroll but missing from Schedule FA: usually the ₹1 lakh category.
- Unreported dividends or sale gains abroad: undisclosed foreign income at 60%.
- Shares valued at the 31 March 2026 high-low average, converted at the RBI rate; deadline 31 December 2026.

Holding RSUs abroad? We map every vest, sale and dividend, choose the right category and file before 31 December.WhatsApp usFree 15-min callHow we file

## Which category applies

The FAQs do not mention RSUs by name, so this follows the category definitions:

- Shares whose vesting was taxed through your Indian payroll but which were never shown in Schedule FA: the asset came from income already taxed, so Category 2 (flat ₹1 lakh, up to ₹5 crore of foreign assets) is the natural fit.

- Dividends, sale gains or interest abroad that you never reported: that is undisclosed foreign income, which falls in Category 1 (60%).

- ESPP shares bought with salary that was taxed in India follow the same logic as RSUs.

Many employees have both: taxed shares that were simply not reported, plus small unreported dividends or gains. Getting the split right is most of the work.

## How the shares are valued

Listed shares are valued at the higher of cost and the average of the highest and lowest price on 31 March 2026, converted to rupees at the RBI reference rate for that day. Cash left in the brokerage account is part of the foreign assets too.

## What to collect

- Vesting statements and payslips showing the perquisite tax on each vest.

- Brokerage statements (E*Trade, Morgan Stanley, Fidelity, Schwab or similar) from the first vest to 31 March 2026.

- Records of sales, dividends and US tax withheld on dividends.

- Your Indian returns for the years concerned.

## After FAST-DS

Report the shares in Schedule FA every year, report dividends and sale gains in your return, and claim credit for US tax withheld on dividends under the India–US treaty. See the India–US tax treaty guide.

## Sources

- Income Tax Department: FAST-DS FAQs (13 August 2026)
- TaxGuru: FAST-DS 2026 FAQs
- Business Today: how FAST-DS 2026 can help fix past omissions (ESOPs, overseas accounts)

## Frequently asked questions
Do I need FAST-DS for RSUs from a foreign employer?
If the RSU shares or the brokerage account were never shown in Schedule FA, FAST-DS is the way to regularise them before 31 December 2026. Where the vesting was taxed through Indian payroll, the shares came from taxed income, which fits the ₹1 lakh category (up to ₹5 crore); unreported dividends or gains are undisclosed foreign income at 60%.

How are RSU shares valued under FAST-DS?
At the higher of cost and the average of the highest and lowest quoted price on 31 March 2026 (or the nearest earlier trading day), converted to rupees at the RBI reference rate for that date.

My RSU tax was deducted by my employer. Why is there a problem?
Because paying the tax is only half of the requirement. Residents must also report foreign assets, including shares and brokerage accounts abroad, in Schedule FA of the return. Leaving them out can attract a ₹10 lakh penalty under the Black Money Act where foreign assets other than property exceed ₹20 lakh.

FAST-DS · Foreign bank accounts

# Foreign bank account not reported? How FAST-DS values it

A US or UK account opened during studies or a posting abroad, still open with a small balance and never shown in Schedule FA, is one of the most common FAST-DS cases. The surprise is how the scheme values it.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 4 November 2026·5 min read

Sort out your foreign account
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Got the email about “overseas financial interests”? What the FAST-DS email means and what to do.
Key takeaways
- FAST-DS values a bank account at the sum of all deposits, not the balance.
- Deposits from non-resident earnings or taxed income: ₹1 lakh flat; from untaxed income: 60%.
- Under ₹20 lakh of non-property foreign assets, the ₹10 lakh penalty generally does not apply; still report them.

Old account abroad? We rebuild the deposit history, choose the category and file before 31 December.WhatsApp usFree 15-min callHow we file

## The sum-of-deposits rule

For FAST-DS, a bank account is valued at the total of all deposits made into it from the day it was opened up to 31 March 2026, not its balance. Deposits made out of withdrawals from the same account are excluded. The total converts to rupees at the RBI reference rate on 31 March 2026.

Example | Amount | 

Balance on 31 March 2026 | US$ 4,900 | 

Total deposits since the account was opened (salary, transfers) | US$ 60,000 | 

Value for FAST-DS | US$ 60,000, converted at the RBI reference rate | 

That is why the choice of category matters so much: in Category 1 you pay 60% of the deposits; in Category 2 a flat ₹1 lakh.

## Which category

- Deposits came from money earned while you were a non-resident (a job or internship abroad), or from income already taxed in India: Category 2, flat ₹1 lakh, if your foreign assets total up to ₹5 crore.

- Deposits came from income that should have been taxed in India but was not: Category 1, 60%, up to ₹1 crore together with any undisclosed income.

## Small, dormant accounts

Since 1 October 2024 the ₹10 lakh Black Money Act penalty for leaving foreign assets out of Schedule FA does not apply where your foreign assets other than immovable property total ₹20 lakh or less. You must still report them. For a genuinely small account funded from taxed or non-resident income, reporting it correctly from now on may be enough; for anything larger or unclear, FAST-DS gives certainty.

## What to do

- Download statements from account opening to 31 March 2026.
- Identify the source of each major deposit.
- Decide the category and compute the value.
- File Form 1 by 31 December 2026, pay after Form 2, file Form 3.
- Report the account in Schedule FA from now on, or close it.

## Sources

- TaxGuru: FAST-DS 2026 FAQs (valuation of bank accounts)
- Business Today: relief from penalty for small foreign assets (₹20 lakh)
- Income Tax Department: FAST-DS FAQs (13 August 2026)

## Frequently asked questions
How is a foreign bank account valued under FAST-DS?
At the sum of all deposits made into it from the date it was opened up to 31 March 2026, excluding deposits made out of withdrawals from the same account, converted at the RBI reference rate. It is not the account balance.

Do I need FAST-DS for a small foreign bank account?
Not necessarily. Since 1 October 2024 the ₹10 lakh penalty for omitting foreign assets from Schedule FA does not apply where your foreign assets other than immovable property total ₹20 lakh or less, but you must still report them. Larger or unclear cases benefit from FAST-DS.

Which FAST-DS category applies to my student or work account abroad?
If the deposits came from money earned while you were a non-resident, or from income already taxed in India, it is the ₹1 lakh category (up to ₹5 crore). If the deposits came from income that should have been taxed in India but was not, it is the 60% category (up to ₹1 crore).

FAST-DS · Returning NRIs

# Back in India? FAST-DS for assets from your years abroad

Once you become resident again, everything you hold abroad (bank accounts, 401(k) or pension, brokerage accounts, a home) has to be shown in Schedule FA every year. Many returning NRIs miss this for a few years. FAST-DS has a category built for exactly that.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 4 November 2026·5 min read

Regularise your foreign assets
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Got the email about “overseas financial interests”? What the FAST-DS email means and what to do.
Key takeaways
- Assets acquired while non-resident and missed in Schedule FA: flat ₹1 lakh (up to ₹5 crore).
- Unreported income after becoming resident: 60% category.
- Check RNOR years; declare by 31 December 2026.

Returned to India? We review your foreign holdings and file the cheapest correct declaration before 31 December.WhatsApp usFree 15-min callHow we file

## The ₹1 lakh route for non-resident years

Category 2 of FAST-DS covers a foreign asset that was acquired when you were a non-resident, or from income already taxed in India, but which was not shown in Schedule FA. The cost is a flat ₹1 lakh as long as your foreign assets total up to ₹5 crore as on 31 March 2026. For most returning NRIs, savings built up while working abroad fall here.

## Where it gets more expensive

- Income earned after you became resident and not reported, such as interest, dividends, rent or gains on those foreign assets: that is undisclosed foreign income, at 60% under Category 1.

- Foreign assets worth more than ₹5 crore: not eligible for FAST-DS.

## RNOR years

In the first years after return you may be “resident but not ordinarily resident” (RNOR), when foreign income is generally not taxed in India. Check your status year by year with the residential status calculator, because it decides which income was actually taxable and which reporting applied.

## Typical holdings

- US 401(k), IRA or UK pension: report in Schedule FA; growth and withdrawals have their own tax rules.

- Bank and brokerage accounts: for banks, FAST-DS uses the sum of deposits, not the balance; see foreign bank accounts.

- A home abroad: needs a valuation report from a recognised valuer in that country.

Planning the move back? See returning to India from the US.

## Sources

- TaxGuru: FAST-DS 2026 FAQs (categories)
- Income Tax Department: FAST-DS FAQs (13 August 2026)
Holding US stocks and moving abroad? What changes for NRIs: tax, Schedule FA and W-8BEN.
Living abroad now? FAST-DS for NRIs in the UK, US, Canada and Australia.

## Frequently asked questions
Can returning NRIs use FAST-DS?
Yes. Assets acquired while you were a non-resident and not shown in Schedule FA after you became resident fall in the ₹1 lakh category, as long as your foreign assets total up to ₹5 crore as on 31 March 2026.

What if I earned income on my foreign assets after returning to India?
Interest, dividends, rent or gains that were taxable in India after you became resident but were not reported are undisclosed foreign income, which falls in the 60% category, up to ₹1 crore together with any undisclosed assets.

Do RNOR years matter for FAST-DS?
Yes. As RNOR, foreign income is generally not taxed in India, which affects whether income was actually undisclosed. Check your residential status for each year before deciding the category.
