Income tax · Updated returns

# ITR-U time limit: last dates and extra tax, year by year

Missed income, a wrong claim, or a year you never filed? An updated return (ITR-U) lets you correct it voluntarily within 48 months of the end of the assessment year, if you pay the tax, interest and an extra tax that rises the longer you wait.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 4 November 2026·4 min read

Fix past years before the rate rises
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Hold anything abroad? FAST-DS 2026 closes on 31 December: a one-time chance to declare foreign accounts, RSUs and assets missed in your returns, from a flat ₹1 lakh. Check what you would pay or get it filed.

Key takeaways
- ITR-U window: 48 months from the end of the assessment year.
- Extra tax: 25%, 50%, 60% or 70% of tax and interest, depending on how late.
- FY 2021-22 closes 31 March 2027; ITR-U cannot be used for refunds or losses.

Closing soon: the window for FY 2021-22 (AY 2022-23) ends on 31 March 2027, and the extra tax for that year is already at the top rate of 70%. For FY 2022-23 (AY 2023-24), it rises from 60% to 70% after 31 March 2027.

## Last dates and current extra tax (as on November 2026)

Financial year (assessment year) | Extra tax if filed now | Rate rises on | Last date for ITR-U | 

2021-22 (AY 2022-23) | 70% | — | 31 March 2027 | 

2022-23 (AY 2023-24) | 60% | 1 April 2027 (to 70%) | 31 March 2028 | 

2023-24 (AY 2024-25) | 50% | 1 April 2027 (to 60%) | 31 March 2029 | 

2024-25 (AY 2025-26) | 25% | 1 April 2027 (to 50%) | 31 March 2030 | 

The extra tax is a percentage of the tax and interest due on the additional income. For FY 2025-26, a belated return can still be filed until 31 December 2026, and a revised return until 31 March 2027 (with a fee of ₹1,000 or ₹5,000 after 31 December). Both are cheaper than an updated return.

## How the extra tax works

Filed within, from the end of the assessment year | Additional tax | 

12 months | 25% | 
12 to 24 months | 50% | 
24 to 36 months | 60% | 
36 to 48 months | 70% | 

## When you cannot file an updated return

- To reduce your tax, increase a refund, or file or increase a loss.

- If a search or survey has been started against you, or an assessment or reassessment for that year is pending or completed.

- Beyond 48 months: older years cannot be fixed with ITR-U.

## “I never filed for several years”

If TDS was deducted and you simply never filed, ITR-U can cover only the last four assessment years, and only where it increases tax or brings in unreported income. Years with excess TDS and no tax due are not helped by ITR-U, because it cannot be used to claim a refund. Older years can still be picked up by the department if it has information, so get the position reviewed year by year. NRIs with Indian TDS often fall into this; see ITR for NRIs.

## How to file

- Work out the additional income and the tax and interest on it.
- Pay the tax, interest and additional tax first.
- File the updated return form on the e-filing portal for that year, with the payment details.
- Keep the computation; the department can still ask questions.

## Sources

- Taxmann: FAQs on updated return of income (ITR-U)
- Business Today: ITR-U deadline extended to 48 months (Budget 2025)
- Income-tax e-filing portal

## Frequently asked questions
What is the last date to file ITR-U for AY 2023-24?
31 March 2028, because an updated return can be filed within 48 months from the end of the assessment year. Filed now, the additional tax is 60%; it rises to 70% from 1 April 2027.

What is the last date for ITR-U for FY 2021-22?
31 March 2027 for AY 2022-23. The additional tax for that year is already at the highest rate of 70% of the tax and interest.

How much extra tax is payable on an updated return?
25% of the tax and interest if filed within 12 months of the end of the assessment year, 50% within 24 months, 60% within 36 months and 70% within 48 months.

Can I file ITR-U to claim a refund?
No. An updated return cannot reduce tax, increase a refund or create or increase a loss. It is only for reporting additional income or correcting errors that increase tax.

FEMA · RBI · October 2026

# FEMA compounding: ODI, ECB and guarantee cases move to RBI regional offices

If your company missed an overseas investment filing, took a foreign loan without following the rules, or gave a guarantee for a foreign subsidiary without reporting it, compounding is how the default is settled. From late October 2026, many of these cases go to RBI regional offices instead of the central office in Mumbai.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 3 November 2026·5 min read

Regularise your FEMA default
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- RBI circular of 23 October 2026: ODI, borrowing/lending and guarantee compounding moved to regional offices.
- ODI cases routed by UIN; borrowing and guarantees by registered office; multi-category or no-UIN cases stay central.
- Late reports within the window: late fee. Beyond it, or substantive breaches: compounding.

Have an old FEMA default? We work out whether a late fee is enough or compounding is needed, and prepare the application.Free 15-min callWhatsApp

Already own a US LLC without Form FC? How to regularise it, step by step.

## What changed

- RBI circular A.P. (DIR Series) No. 28/2026-27, dated 23 October 2026, delegates compounding of contraventions relating to overseas investment, borrowing and lending and guarantees to selected regional offices.

- Which office: overseas investment cases go by the foreign entity’s UIN; borrowing, lending and guarantee cases go to the office covering the applicant’s registered office or domicile.

- What stays in Mumbai: applications without a UIN, or covering several categories at once, are still handled by the Foreign Exchange Department’s compounding cell (CEFA) at RBI’s central office.

- The office-wise jurisdiction table is in the Master Direction on Compounding of Contraventions under FEMA, 1999 (22 April 2025), which RBI is updating.

## Late fee or compounding?

Situation | Usual route | 

A report filed late (for example Form FC, APR, FC-GPR) within the window the rules allow | Pay a late submission fee; see the LSF calculator | 

Reporting so late that the late-fee route is no longer available | Compounding | 

A substantive breach: investing without the required approval, a foreign loan outside the borrowing rules, an unreported guarantee | Compounding | 

## How compounding works

- Map every contravention with dates and amounts; RBI wants the full picture in one application.

- File the compounding application with the documents and the application fee, to the right office.

- RBI computes the compounding amount under the Master Direction, based on the amount and the period of the contravention.

- Pay within the time given; the contravention is then treated as settled, and no further proceedings follow for it.

## Who should act now

- Indian companies with foreign subsidiaries whose APRs or Form FC were missed in past years.

- Companies that gave guarantees or loans to overseas group companies without reporting them.

- Companies that raised foreign loans without completing the borrowing formalities.

- Groups planning a fundraise, IPO or sale: investors’ due diligence will find these defaults, and compounding before the deal is cheaper and faster than explaining them during it.

Related: APR and audit for overseas subsidiaries, ODI rules for US companies and FEMA / RBI compliance.

## Sources

- TaxGuru: FEMA compounding for overseas investments, loans and guarantees delegated to regional offices
- Sansa Legal: RBI sends FEMA compounding to regional offices
- AK & Partners: Banking & Finance Digest, 2 November 2026

## Frequently asked questions
What did RBI change about FEMA compounding in October 2026?
Circular A.P. (DIR Series) No. 28/2026-27 of 23 October 2026 delegated compounding of contraventions relating to overseas investment, borrowing and lending, and guarantees to selected RBI regional offices. Cases without a UIN or covering several categories stay with the central office.

Which RBI office handles my compounding application?
For overseas investment, the office mapped to the foreign entity's UIN; for borrowing, lending and guarantees, the office covering your registered office or domicile. The jurisdiction table is in the Master Direction on Compounding of Contraventions under FEMA.

Do I need compounding or just a late submission fee?
A late report filed within the window the rules allow can usually be regularised with a late submission fee. Reporting beyond that window, and substantive breaches such as investing without approval or unreported guarantees, need compounding.

Is compounding a penalty?
It is a voluntary settlement: you admit the contravention and pay a compounding amount computed by RBI, and the matter is closed without adjudication proceedings.

Cross-border tax · Software

# TDS on software and SaaS paid to foreign companies

Almost every Indian business now pays a foreign company for software: cloud, CRM, design tools, enterprise licences. The question accountants keep asking is whether TDS applies when the money goes to, say, Oracle Singapore or AWS. Usually it does not, but only if the paperwork is in place.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 3 November 2026·5 min read

Check your foreign payment
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- Standard software licences and SaaS from a foreign vendor with no Indian PE: generally no TDS under treaty.
- Keep the vendor's TRC and Form 41; file Forms 145/146 (formerly 15CA/15CB) where required.
- Customised software, technical services or an Indian PE can change the answer; equalisation levy has been abolished.

Paying a foreign vendor? We confirm the TDS position, get the vendor's Form 41 and TRC, and file Forms 145/146.Free 15-min callWhatsApp

## Short answer

For most standard software licences and SaaS subscriptions bought from a foreign company with no permanent establishment in India, the payment is not taxable in India under the tax treaty, so no TDS is needed. You still need the vendor’s tax residency certificate and Form 41 (formerly Form 10F) on file, and the remittance paperwork (Forms 145/146, formerly 15CA/15CB) where the bank requires it.

## Why: the Supreme Court software ruling

In Engineering Analysis Centre of Excellence v CIT (2 March 2021), the Supreme Court held that paying for the use of software under an end-user licence or a distribution agreement is not a payment for the use of copyright, so it is not “royalty” under India’s tax treaties. Without royalty, and without a permanent establishment in India, the foreign vendor’s income is not taxable in India, and there is nothing to deduct tax from.

## Which payments are different

Payment | Usual position | 

Standard licence or SaaS subscription (cloud, CRM, productivity, design) | Generally not taxable in India under treaty; no TDS with TRC and Form 41 | 

Software customised for you, or with source-code or copyright rights transferred | May be royalty; check the treaty rate | 

Implementation, consulting or support by the vendor’s people | May be fees for technical services; some treaties (for example US, UK, Singapore) tax these only if they “make available” know-how | 

Vendor has an office, staff or dependent agent in India | Possible permanent establishment; TDS may apply | 

## Equalisation levy is gone

The 2% equalisation levy on e-commerce supplies was abolished from 1 August 2024, and the 6% levy on online advertising from 1 April 2025. There is no separate levy to deduct on these payments now.

## What to do, step by step

- Classify the payment: licence, subscription, service or customised software.

- Collect from the vendor: tax residency certificate, Form 41 (they file it online, no PAN needed) and a no-PE declaration.

- If not taxable: no TDS; file Form 145 (formerly 15CA) and get Form 146 (formerly 15CB) where required by the remittance rules and your bank.

- If taxable: deduct under section 393(2) of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (formerly 195) at the treaty or Act rate, deposit it, report it in Form 144 (formerly 27Q) and issue Form 131.

- GST: a GST-registered business importing online services pays GST under reverse charge and can usually claim the input credit.

Related: TDS on payments to non-residents, Form 41 and no-PE declaration and GST on foreign SaaS.

## Sources

- ITAT Online: Engineering Analysis Centre of Excellence v CIT (Supreme Court, 2 March 2021), full text
- Income Tax Department: Form 41 FAQs
- Income-tax e-filing portal

## Frequently asked questions
Is TDS required on payment to a foreign software company?
Usually not for standard software licences or SaaS subscriptions from a foreign company with no permanent establishment in India: after the Supreme Court's 2021 Engineering Analysis ruling, these are not royalty under tax treaties, so the income is not taxable in India. Keep the vendor's tax residency certificate and Form 41, and file Forms 145/146 where required.

Do I need to deduct TDS on AWS or Microsoft subscriptions paid abroad?
Generally no, if the payment is a standard cloud or software subscription to a foreign entity without a permanent establishment in India and you hold its tax residency certificate and Form 41. Payments to an Indian entity of the same group follow domestic TDS rules instead.

Is equalisation levy still payable on foreign software or ads?
No. The 2% equalisation levy on e-commerce supplies ended from 1 August 2024 and the 6% levy on online advertising ended from 1 April 2025.

Is GST payable on SaaS bought from a foreign company?
Yes. A GST-registered business importing online services pays GST under reverse charge, usually with input tax credit. For unregistered buyers, the foreign supplier charges GST.

Please note: this guide is general information based on the rules as they stood on the review date above. Regulations and RBI/CBDT procedures change often — please get advice on your specific facts before acting.

NRI tax · 2026-27

# NRI income tax slab 2026-27: rates, the missing rebate and your refund

NRIs pay Indian tax only on income earned or received in India, at the same slab rates as residents, with two big differences: no ₹12 lakh rebate, and TDS that is usually far higher than the tax actually due.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 3 November 2026·4 min read

Claim your NRI refund
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Hold anything abroad? FAST-DS 2026 closes on 31 December: a one-time chance to declare foreign accounts, RSUs and assets missed in your returns, from a flat ₹1 lakh. Check what you would pay or get it filed.

Key takeaways
- NRI slabs 2026-27 (new regime): nil to ₹4 lakh, then 5% to 30% in ₹4 lakh steps above.
- No ₹12 lakh rebate for NRIs; old-regime exemption is ₹2.5 lakh at any age.
- Bank TDS on NRO interest is 31.2%; most NRIs get a refund by filing a return.

Had TDS deducted on your NRO interest, rent or gains? Most NRIs are owed a refund. We file your Indian return and claim it.Ask on WhatsAppFree 15-min call

Work out your own tax: NRI income tax calculator, new vs old regime, with your refund against TDS.

## New regime slabs for NRIs (2026-27)

Taxable income | Rate | 

Up to ₹4 lakh | Nil | 
₹4 lakh to ₹8 lakh | 5% | 
₹8 lakh to ₹12 lakh | 10% | 
₹12 lakh to ₹16 lakh | 15% | 
₹16 lakh to ₹20 lakh | 20% | 
₹20 lakh to ₹24 lakh | 25% | 
Above ₹24 lakh | 30% | 

Plus 4% health and education cess, and surcharge on high incomes (10% above ₹50 lakh, 15% above ₹1 crore, 25% above ₹2 crore under the new regime). The ₹75,000 standard deduction applies if you have Indian salary or pension.

## No ₹12 lakh rebate for NRIs

Residents with income up to ₹12 lakh pay no tax because of the rebate (section 156 of the Income-tax Act, 2025, formerly section 87A). That rebate is only for residents. An NRI with ₹10 lakh of Indian income pays tax from the first rupee above ₹4 lakh.

## Old regime for NRIs

NRIs can still choose the old regime, with its deductions. The basic exemption is ₹2.5 lakh at any age: the higher limits for senior citizens apply only to residents.

## Special rates that apply regardless of slab

Income | Tax for NRIs | 

Listed shares and equity funds, held up to 12 months | 20% | 

Listed shares and equity funds, held over 12 months | 12.5% above ₹1.25 lakh a year | 

Property held over 24 months | 12.5% without indexation (the indexation option for property bought before 23 July 2024 is for residents only) | 

Interest on NRE deposits | Exempt | 

## Example: why most NRIs are owed a refund

NRI with ₹10 lakh interest on an NRO fixed deposit | Amount | 

TDS deducted by the bank (30% plus 4% cess) | ₹3,12,000 | 

Actual tax under the new regime: 5% on ₹4 to ₹8 lakh, 10% on ₹8 to ₹10 lakh, plus cess | ₹41,600 | 

Refund if you file an Indian return | ₹2,70,400 | 

A treaty rate can cut the TDS itself: for example, India’s treaties with the UAE, UK and US cap tax on interest, if you give the bank a tax residency certificate and Form 41. Either way, filing the return is how you get the excess back. See filing an ITR as an NRI.

## Who counts as an NRI?

Broadly, you are a non-resident for a year if you are in India for less than 182 days (with extra tests for some visitors and high earners). Check with the residential status calculator. Moved recently? See the NRI checklist for the UAE and the full NRI taxation guide.

## Sources

- Income-tax e-filing portal
- Income Tax Department: Form 41 FAQs (treaty rates for non-residents)
- Consulate General of India, Dubai: CBDT clarification on tax residency of NRIs

## Frequently asked questions
What is the income tax slab for NRIs in 2026-27?
Under the new regime: nil up to ₹4 lakh, 5% from ₹4 to ₹8 lakh, 10% from ₹8 to ₹12 lakh, 15% from ₹12 to ₹16 lakh, 20% from ₹16 to ₹20 lakh, 25% from ₹20 to ₹24 lakh and 30% above ₹24 lakh, plus 4% cess and surcharge on high incomes.

Do NRIs get the ₹12 lakh tax rebate?
No. The rebate that makes income up to ₹12 lakh tax-free (section 156 of the Income-tax Act, 2025, formerly 87A) is available only to residents. NRIs pay tax on Indian income above ₹4 lakh under the new regime.

What is the basic exemption limit for NRIs?
₹4 lakh under the new regime and ₹2.5 lakh under the old regime, at any age. The higher old-regime limits for senior citizens apply only to residents.

Can an NRI get a refund of TDS on NRO interest?
Usually yes. Banks deduct 30% plus cess on NRO interest, which is often far more than the slab tax due. Filing an Indian income tax return claims the excess back; a treaty rate with a tax residency certificate and Form 41 can also reduce the TDS.

FEMA · ODI · Due 31 December

# APR for an overseas subsidiary: do you need an audit?

If an Indian company or resident owns a foreign company, it must file an Annual Performance Report (APR) with its bank every year. The question that trips most groups up: does the foreign subsidiary need audited accounts when its own country does not require an audit?

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 3 November 2026·5 min read

Get your APR done before 31 December
hello@durgeshchavda.com

APRs missed in past years? late fee or compounding.
Key takeaways
- APR due 31 December 2026 through your AD bank.
- Controlled subsidiary = audited statements needed, even if the host country requires no audit.
- Unaudited (certified) statements only if no control and no host-country audit requirement.

APR due 31 December 2026. We prepare the subsidiary's financials and the APR, and coordinate the audit with a practising auditor.Free 15-min callWhatsAppEmail

Already own a US LLC without Form FC? How to regularise it, step by step.

## Short answer

If you control the foreign entity, you need audited financial statements for the APR, even if the host country (for example Delaware or many US states) does not require an audit. Unaudited statements are allowed only when both conditions hold: the Indian investor does not have control, and the host country does not mandate an audit. In that case, the unaudited statements are certified by the statutory auditor of the Indian entity, or by a chartered accountant where no statutory audit applies.

## When is the APR due?

By 31 December every year, through your authorised dealer (AD) bank, based on the foreign entity’s accounts for the year ending in the previous calendar year (for most groups, the year to 31 March). For a subsidiary with a March 2026 year end, the APR is due by 31 December 2026. Late filing attracts a late submission fee; see the FEMA late submission fee calculator.

## Which case are you?

Situation | Basis for the APR | 

Wholly owned or controlled subsidiary, host country requires audit (for example UK companies above the small-company exemption) | Audited statements under host-country law | 

Wholly owned or controlled subsidiary, no audit required locally (for example most Delaware corporations) | Audited statements still needed; a special purpose audit for APR is common | 

Minority stake without control, no local audit requirement | Unaudited statements certified by the Indian entity’s statutory auditor or a CA | 

## How groups get it done

- Prepare the foreign entity’s financial statements in its own currency, from the same books used for consolidation.

- Arrange the audit. Where no local audit exists, groups commonly have a special purpose audit of those statements done for APR and banking purposes. Ask your AD bank in advance which auditor it will accept.

- Prepare and file the APR with the AD bank, with the audited statements and the foreign entity’s key figures.

- Keep the rest of ODI reporting current: Form FC for any new remittance, and the annual FLA return where applicable.

## Common mistakes

- Assuming “no US audit requirement” means “no audit for the APR”.

- Filing the APR on INR consolidation figures instead of the subsidiary’s own statements.

- Leaving it to December, when auditors and banks are busiest.

- Missing APRs for dormant or loss-making subsidiaries; they still need one.

Related: FEMA and ODI rules when Indians own a US company and FEMA / RBI compliance.

## Sources

- RBI: Form APR and instructions (Overseas Investment, 2022)
- RBI: Foreign Exchange Management (Overseas Investment) Regulations, 2022
- Compliance Calendar: audit requirement for APR filing

## Frequently asked questions
Is an audit required for the APR of an overseas subsidiary?
Yes, if the Indian investor has control. The APR must then be based on audited financial statements even where the host country does not require an audit. Unaudited statements, certified by the Indian entity's statutory auditor or a chartered accountant, are allowed only when the investor has no control and the host country does not mandate an audit.

What is the due date for the APR in 2026?
31 December 2026 for foreign entities whose accounting year ended in 2026 up to that point, for most groups the year to 31 March 2026. It is filed through the authorised dealer bank.

Does a Delaware subsidiary of an Indian company need an audit?
Delaware law does not generally require a private corporation to be audited, but if the Indian parent controls it, the APR still needs audited financial statements, so a special purpose audit is usually done for the APR and bank.

What happens if the APR is filed late?
A late submission fee applies under the overseas investment rules, and the AD bank may restrict further overseas remittances until reporting is regularised. It is cheaper to file on time.

NRI · UAE · New residents

# Moved from India to Dubai? Your NRI checklist

Moving to the UAE for work changes your status under Indian tax and foreign exchange law, and almost every account you hold in India has to be updated. Here is the order to do it in, investment by investment.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 3 November 2026·6 min read

Get your move sorted
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Hold anything abroad? FAST-DS 2026 closes on 31 December: a one-time chance to declare foreign accounts, RSUs and assets missed in your returns, from a flat ₹1 lakh. Check what you would pay or get it filed.

Key takeaways
- Non-resident if in India less than 182 days in the year (employment abroad).
- Re-designate savings to NRO, open NRE, convert demat; update MFs, EPF, NPS, SGBs and insurance.
- Only Indian-source income is taxed in India; file a return to recover excess TDS.

Just moved? We review your residential status and every holding, then take you through each change with your bank, broker and fund houses.Free 15-min callWhatsAppEmail

## 1. Your residential status

- An Indian citizen who leaves India for employment abroad is a non-resident for a financial year if in India for less than 182 days in that year. The year you leave is usually still a resident year if you spent 182 days or more in India before leaving.

- There is a deemed-residency rule for Indian citizens with high Indian income who are not taxed anywhere else. The CBDT has said it is not meant to catch citizens who are bona fide workers in other countries, such as in the UAE, where there is no personal income tax. Keep your UAE employment contract and Emirates ID.

- Count your days with the residential status calculator.

## 2. Bank accounts (FEMA)

- Tell each bank you are now non-resident. Resident savings accounts must be re-designated as NRO accounts; banks generally expect this promptly after you leave.

- Open an NRE account for money you earn abroad: balances and interest are repatriable and NRE interest is tax-free in India.

- Indian income such as rent, dividends and interest goes into the NRO account. You can send up to USD 1 million a financial year abroad from NRO balances, with Forms 145 and 146 (formerly 15CA and 15CB) where required.

## 3. Investments, one by one

Holding | What to do | 

Shares and demat (for example Zerodha) | A resident demat cannot continue as is. Convert to an NRI demat and trading account linked to your NRE (repatriable, through PIS) or NRO (non-repatriable) bank account, and transfer the holdings. | 

Mutual funds and SIPs | Update your tax status to NRI with each fund house or registrar, update your bank mandate to an NRE/NRO account, and complete NRI KYC. UAE residents can generally continue investing. | 

Smallcase and other broker platforms | Follow the broker’s NRI process once your demat is converted; some products are not open to NRIs. | 

EPF | Your account can stay. Update your status and bank details; check the tax on interest and the rules before withdrawing. | 

NPS | NRIs can continue NPS. Update your status, address and bank account with your NPS provider. | 

Sovereign Gold Bonds | Bonds bought while resident can be held until early redemption or maturity. Interest (2.5% a year) is taxable in India. Check the capital gains position before selling. | 

ULIPs and life insurance | Update your residential status and address with the insurer; premiums can be paid from NRE or NRO accounts. Check the tax on maturity for high-premium policies. | 

Crypto (for example CoinDCX) | Check whether the exchange allows NRI accounts. Gains on crypto are taxed at 30% in India, and TDS applies on transfers. | 

Nothing needs to be sold just because you moved. The aim is to re-paper each holding so it stays compliant and you can bring the money out later.

## 4. Indian tax from now on

- As a non-resident, only income earned or received in India is taxable in India: interest, rent, dividends, capital gains on Indian assets. Your UAE salary is not taxed in India.

- Banks, brokers and fund houses will deduct TDS at NRI rates, often higher than your actual tax. File an Indian return to claim refunds; see ITR for NRIs.

- The India–UAE tax treaty can lower tax on some income; you will need a UAE tax residency certificate.

- Your PAN stays valid; NRIs are not required to link PAN with Aadhaar, but update your status with the tax department so your PAN is not treated as inoperative.

## The order to do it in

- Confirm your residential status for the year.
- Re-designate bank accounts and open NRE/NRO.
- Convert demat and trading accounts.
- Update mutual funds, EPF, NPS, insurance and SGB records.
- Check each platform you use for NRI eligibility.
- Plan your first NRI tax return.

Related: NRI tax services, a CA for Indians in Dubai and NRI taxation guide.

## Sources

- Consulate General of India, Dubai: CBDT clarification on deemed tax residency (Feb 2020)
- RBI: Foreign Exchange Management (Deposit) Regulations, 2016 (NRE/NRO)
- IDFC FIRST Bank: impact of residential status on Indian investments
Holding US stocks and moving abroad? What changes for NRIs: tax, Schedule FA and W-8BEN.
Shares and mutual funds in India? Demat and mutual funds after becoming an NRI.

## Frequently asked questions
What should I do with my Indian bank account after moving to Dubai?
Tell the bank you are now non-resident and have your resident savings account re-designated as an NRO account. Open an NRE account for money earned in the UAE; NRE balances are repatriable and the interest is tax-free in India.

Can I keep my Zerodha account after becoming an NRI?
Not as a resident account. You need to convert it to an NRI demat and trading account linked to an NRE account (repatriable, through PIS) or an NRO account (non-repatriable), and move your holdings across.

Can an NRI in the UAE continue mutual fund SIPs?
Generally yes. Update your tax status to NRI with each fund house, complete NRI KYC and change the bank mandate to an NRE or NRO account. Some fund houses restrict investors in certain countries, but the UAE is usually accepted.

Can I keep Sovereign Gold Bonds after becoming an NRI?
Yes. Bonds bought while you were resident can be held until early redemption or maturity. The 2.5% interest is taxable in India.

Is my UAE salary taxed in India?
No, not once you are a non-resident. Non-residents are taxed in India only on income earned or received in India, such as Indian interest, rent, dividends and capital gains.

FEMA · Exports · Updated 10 November 2026

# EDF for services: what freelancers, SaaS and creators need now

Banks started asking service exporters for an Export Declaration Form (EDF) in October 2026. RBI then eased the rule on 2 November 2026, with effect from 1 October: for individual freelancers and receipts up to ₹10 lakh, the EDF is now treated as filed once you give the bank the payment details. Here is who still files, and how to handle invoices and remitter mismatches.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 10 November 2026·5 min read

Get your EDFs sorted
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- From 1 October 2026, a freelancer's EDF is deemed submitted once the bank has the payment details. No value limit for individuals.
- Companies and firms: deemed filing for receipts up to ₹10 lakh; above that, file the EDF as before.
- Keep invoices and the bank advice; payments are still due within nine months.

Payment stuck at the bank? We prepare your invoices and EDFs and deal with the bank, so your foreign receipts are credited.Free 15-min callWhatsAppEmail

## New: deemed EDF from 1 October 2026

RBI amended the rules on 2 November 2026 (Notification No. FEMA 23(R)/(2)/2026-RB), with effect from 1 October 2026. For most freelancers and small exporters, the separate EDF is no longer needed:

Who you are | EDF for services | 

Resident individual (freelancer, consultant, creator working in your own name) | Deemed submitted once you give the bank the details it needs about the payment to credit your account. No value limit. | 

Company, LLP, firm or other non-individual, receipt up to ₹10 lakh | Deemed submitted where the inward remittance for the service is not more than ₹10 lakh (or the foreign-currency equivalent), again on giving the bank the payment details. | 

Non-individual, receipt above ₹10 lakh | File the EDF with your bank as before. | 

- “Deemed” is not “nothing to do”. The deeming works only when you give the bank complete payment details. Keep the invoice, the client and service description, and the bank’s inward remittance advice for every receipt.

- How the ₹10 lakh is measured: the notification refers to the value of the inward remittance for the service. Commentators read it as per remittance, not a yearly turnover test; it does not say how a single payment covering several invoices is treated. Ask your bank how it applies it.

- Payment deadlines are unchanged: export proceeds should still be received within nine months.

- Paying for imported services? The bank now enters import-of-services details in IDPMS only where the importer is not a resident individual and the invoice or contract is above ₹10 lakh.

- If your bank still asks for an EDF for an October 2026 receipt, point it to the 2 November 2026 amendment.

## The October 2026 rules (background)

- RBI’s Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2026 replaced the old export rules. Service exports, not just software, were brought under an export declaration with the bank. The 2 November amendment above now deems that declaration filed in most small cases.

- One EDF can cover all of a month’s service invoices, filed within 30 days of the end of the month in which the invoices are raised. For October 2026 invoices, that is by 30 November 2026.

- You file with your bank (the AD bank); the bank reports to RBI. Export proceeds should normally be received within nine months of the invoice.

## “Google or Upwork doesn’t give me an invoice”

You make the invoice yourself. It does not need to come from the payer.

- Your details: name, address, PAN, and GSTIN if registered.

- Billed to: the entity you contract with. For AdSense in India this is Google Asia Pacific Pte. Ltd., Singapore; for marketplaces, check your platform terms.

- Service, period and amount in the foreign currency, matching the payment.

- Invoice number and date, and your LUT reference if you are under GST.

## When the remitter name doesn’t match

Banks often insist that the name on the invoice matches the remitter in the SWIFT message. Platform payments come from a payment entity (for example an escrow or payments company), not from your client. A practical fix is one monthly invoice addressed to the remitter exactly as it appears in the SWIFT message, describing the services delivered through the platform, with an annexure listing each underlying client invoice and the platform’s transaction statement. Confirm with your bank before you rely on it.

## GST and income tax still apply

- If you are GST-registered, file an LUT so your exports are zero-rated, and report them in GSTR-1. See GST on export of services and LUT.

- Export income is taxable in India like any other income; keep the bank’s inward remittance advice (e-FIRA) with your invoices.

## Monthly checklist (exporters still filing EDFs)

- Raise invoices for all foreign clients or platforms for the month.
- Match each payment to an invoice and the SWIFT remitter.
- File one EDF for the month with your bank within 30 days of month-end.
- Keep the e-FIRA, invoices and EDF acknowledgement together.

## Sources

- TaxGuru: RBI relaxes FEMA EDF and IDPMS reporting for services (notification text, 2 Nov 2026)
- CorpLawUpdates: EDF deemed submitted for service exporters (3 Nov 2026)
- EY: RBI issues Export and Import of Goods and Services Regulations, 2026
- LKS: RBI releases FEMA 2026 export-import regulations
- Skydo: EDF filing guide 2026 for service exporters
- Google AdSense Help: contracting entity and tax invoices

## Frequently asked questions
Do freelancers still need to file an EDF?
Not separately, from 1 October 2026. Under RBI's amendment of 2 November 2026, a resident individual exporting services is deemed to have submitted the EDF once they give their bank the information needed about the payment to credit their account. There is no value limit for individuals.

What is the Rs 10 lakh EDF limit for companies?
Companies, LLPs, firms and other non-individual service exporters are deemed to have submitted the EDF where the inward remittance for the service is not more than Rs 10 lakh or its foreign-currency equivalent. Above that, they file the EDF with their bank as before.

What is the EDF deadline for October 2026 invoices?
For exporters who still file (non-individuals with receipts above Rs 10 lakh), the EDF for a month's service invoices is due within 30 days from the end of that month, so 30 November 2026 for October invoices. Individuals and smaller receipts are deemed to have filed under RBI's 2 November 2026 amendment.

How do I create an invoice for AdSense income?
Make it yourself: your name, address and PAN, billed to Google Asia Pacific Pte. Ltd., Singapore (the AdSense contracting entity for India), describing the publisher services for the month, with the amount in US dollars matching the payment, an invoice number and date, and your LUT reference if GST-registered.

My bank says the invoice name must match the SWIFT remitter. What do I do?
Address a monthly invoice to the remitter exactly as named in the SWIFT message, describe the services delivered through the platform, and attach an annexure listing the underlying client invoices and the platform statement. Check with your bank that it will accept this.

For CPA and UK firms

# How to choose an offshore accounting partner: 12 questions to ask

Most offshore arrangements that fail do so for predictable reasons: unclear quality standards, weak access control, staff turnover or no way out. These twelve questions surface those risks before you sign.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 2 November 2026·5 min read

Put these questions to us
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- Test quality with a pilot on three to five real files before signing.
- Insist on work inside your own systems, with logins you control and written security controls.
- US: Section 7216 consent, SSN safeguards and PTINs. UK: an IDTA and transfer risk assessment.

## Quality

- Who will actually do the work, and who reviews it? Ask for the qualifications of the named team (for example Chartered Accountants or CPAs) and how many review layers sit between preparer and you.

- Will you work to our checklists and software? A good partner adapts to your workpaper standards and tools rather than asking you to adopt theirs.

- Can we run a paid or free pilot on real files? Three to five files from your current workload tell you more than any sales call.

- What turnaround do you commit to in busy season? Ask how capacity scales between February and April, not just in quiet months.

## Security and compliance

- Where will our data sit? The safest answer is “in your systems”: your remote desktop, portal and software, with logins you create and can revoke.

- What controls do you have, in writing? Multi-factor authentication, device policy, no local downloads or USB storage, access logs, and any independent attestation such as SOC 2 or ISO 27001 if they have one.

- US firms: how do you handle Section 7216 and PTINs? They should expect you to collect 7216 consents, mask SSNs unless safeguards allow otherwise, and have PTINs for preparers. See the 7216 and PTIN checklist.

- UK firms: will you sign an IDTA? Transfers of personal data to India need a safeguard such as the International Data Transfer Agreement or the UK Addendum, plus a transfer risk assessment.

## People and continuity

- Will we have a named, stable team? Ask about staff turnover and what happens when someone leaves mid-season.

- What are the overlap hours? India is 10 hours 30 minutes ahead of New York in winter and 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of London, so agree a daily overlap window for questions.

## Contract and exit

- How is the fee set? Per return, per hour or a fixed monthly fee, agreed upfront, with clear rules for rework.

- How do we leave? Notice period, return of all working papers, deletion of any data, and no lock-in beyond a reasonable notice period.

## Red flags

- They want client files emailed or downloaded to their own machines.

- They offer to sign or e-file returns themselves, or to act as the client’s agent without being asked.

- No pilot, only a long contract.

- They cannot name who will work on your files.

Want to put these questions to us? See outsourced accounting for CPA firms or for UK practices, and book a free 15-minute call.

## Sources

- IRS: Section 7216 frequently asked questions
- ICO: International data transfer agreement and guidance
- The CPA Journal: considerations for tax return preparers outsourcing overseas (Aug 2025)

## Frequently asked questions
What should I ask an offshore accounting firm before hiring them?
Ask who does and reviews the work, whether they work in your systems and checklists, whether they will run a pilot on real files, their busy-season turnaround, their written security controls, how they handle Section 7216 and PTINs (US) or an IDTA (UK), staff continuity, overlap hours, fees and how you can exit.

Is it safe to outsource accounting to India?
It can be, if the partner works only inside your systems with logins you control, uses multi-factor authentication, keeps no files on local machines, and the legal safeguards are in place: Section 7216 consent and SSN safeguards for US returns, or an IDTA for UK personal data.

Should I start with a pilot when outsourcing accounting?
Yes. A pilot on three to five real files from your current workload shows quality, communication and turnaround before you commit to a longer arrangement.

UK tax · 2025-26 returns

# Self assessment deadline: 31 January 2027

Online self assessment returns for the 2025-26 tax year, and any tax still owed, are due by 31 January 2027. That date falls on a Sunday this time, but the deadline does not move. Here are the dates, payments and penalties to plan around.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 2 November 2026·4 min read

Get help before 31 January
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- 2025-26 online returns and tax due 31 January 2027; file by 30 December 2026 to pay under £3,000 through PAYE.
- Payments on account: half of last year's bill on 31 January and 31 July if the bill was £1,000 or more.
- Late filing: £100, then £10 a day after three months, then 5% or £300 at six and 12 months.

## Key dates for 2025-26 returns

Date | What happens | 

31 October 2026 | Paper return deadline (passed) | 

30 December 2026 | File online by this date to have tax owed of less than £3,000 collected through your PAYE tax code, if you are employed or get a pension | 

31 January 2027 | Online return due; pay the balance for 2025-26 and the first payment on account for 2026-27 | 

31 July 2027 | Second payment on account for 2026-27 | 

## Payments on account

If your last self assessment bill was £1,000 or more, HMRC usually expects two advance payments towards the next year, each half of the previous year’s bill, due on 31 January and 31 July. You do not have to make them if more than 80% of your tax was collected at source, for example through PAYE. If your income has fallen, you can apply to reduce them, but you will pay interest if the reduction turns out to be too much.

## Late-filing penalties

How late | Penalty | 

1 day | £100, even if there is no tax to pay | 

3 months | £10 a day for up to 90 days (up to £900) | 

6 months | 5% of the tax due or £300, whichever is higher | 

12 months | A further 5% or £300, whichever is higher | 

Late payment brings interest at the Bank of England base rate plus 4% and separate late-payment penalties. If you have a reasonable excuse, you can appeal a penalty.

## How this fits with MTD for Income Tax

Making Tax Digital for Income Tax started on 6 April 2026, so it covers the 2026-27 tax year. The 2025-26 return due on 31 January 2027 is filed in the usual way, even if you are already sending quarterly updates. See MTD for Income Tax: quarterly updates.

## For accountancy practices: the January crunch

January is when unfiled returns, missing records and payments on account all land together, this year alongside a February MTD quarterly update. Practices that move record-chasing and first drafts earlier, often to an offshore team, spend January reviewing instead of preparing. See outsourced accounting for UK practices.

Living in the UK with income in India? See the guide for Indians in the UK.

## Sources

- GOV.UK: Self Assessment tax returns, deadlines
- GOV.UK: Self Assessment tax returns, penalties
- GOV.UK: Understand your Self Assessment tax bill, payments on account
- GOV.UK: Pay your Self Assessment tax bill through your tax code

## Frequently asked questions
When is the self assessment deadline in 2027?
31 January 2027 for online 2025-26 returns and for paying the balance of 2025-26 tax and the first payment on account for 2026-27. The date falls on a Sunday but the deadline does not move.

What is the penalty for filing self assessment late?
£100 straight away, then £10 a day for up to 90 days after three months, then 5% of the tax due or £300 (whichever is higher) at six months and again at 12 months. Interest and late-payment penalties apply to unpaid tax.

Can I pay my self assessment tax through my tax code?
Yes, if you owe less than £3,000, are employed or receive a pension, and file your return online by 30 December 2026.

Who has to make payments on account?
Anyone whose last self assessment bill was £1,000 or more, unless more than 80% of their tax was collected at source. Each payment is half of the previous year's bill, due on 31 January and 31 July.

Please note: this guide is general information based on the rules as they stood on the review date above. Regulations and RBI/CBDT procedures change often — please get advice on your specific facts before acting.

US tax · 2027 season

# US tax deadlines 2027: the busy-season calendar

The 2027 filing season covers tax year 2026 and is the first under the new $2,000 threshold for Forms 1099-NEC and 1099-MISC. Here are the dates for calendar-year filers, with weekend roll-forwards already applied.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 1 November 2026·4 min read

Plan your busy-season capacity
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- W-2 and 1099-NEC due Monday 1 Feb 2027; 1065 and 1120-S Monday 15 Mar; 1040 and 1120 Thursday 15 Apr.
- Extensions run to 15 Sep (1065, 1120-S) and 15 Oct (1040, 1120, FBAR).
- 1099-NEC/MISC threshold is $2,000 for payments made in 2026; 1099-K back to $20,000 and 200 transactions.

## 2027 filing calendar (tax year 2026, calendar-year filers)

Date | What is due | 

Friday 15 January 2027 | Fourth-quarter 2026 estimated tax payment | 

Monday 1 February 2027 | Forms W-2 and 1099-NEC to recipients and the IRS/SSA; 1099-MISC to recipients; Q4 Forms 941 and annual 940 (31 January falls on a Sunday) | 

Monday 15 March 2027 | Form 1065 (partnerships) and Form 1120-S (S corporations), with K-1s; Form 7004 to extend | 

Wednesday 31 March 2027 | Electronically filed 1099-MISC and most other information returns (other than 1099-NEC) to the IRS | 

Thursday 15 April 2027 | Form 1040 and Form 1120 (calendar-year C corporations), with Form 5472 where required; Form 4868 or 7004 to extend; first-quarter 2027 estimated tax; FBAR (FinCEN 114), with an automatic extension to 15 October | 

Wednesday 15 September 2027 | Extended Forms 1065 and 1120-S | 

Friday 15 October 2027 | Extended Forms 1040 and 1120; extended FBAR | 

Fiscal-year filers and state returns have their own dates. Check state calendars separately.

## What is new for the 2027 season

- 1099-NEC and 1099-MISC threshold: $2,000. Under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, the reporting threshold rose from $600 to $2,000 for payments made in 2026, and will be adjusted for inflation from 2027. Vendor lists built on the old $600 rule will over-report.

- 1099-K: back to $20,000 and 200 transactions. Payment platforms report only above both limits, so fewer clients will receive one, but income is still taxable without a form.

## How firms spread the load

When | Work to get ahead of | 

November to December | Bookkeeping catch-up for business clients, W-9 collection, engagement letters and Section 7216 consents for any offshore work | 

January | 1099 vendor listings against the $2,000 threshold, payroll year-end, organizers out | 

February to mid-March | Partnership and S-corporation returns and K-1s | 

Mid-March to April | Individual and C-corporation returns; extensions for anything incomplete | 

May to October | Extended returns, amended returns, planning | 

Firms that use an offshore team usually hand over the data-entry-heavy work (bookkeeping clean-up, 1099 listings, trial balance to return, first drafts) and keep review and signature in-house. See outsourced accounting and tax prep for CPA firms and the 7216 and PTIN checklist.

## Sources

- IRS: Publication 509, Tax Calendars
- CPA Practice Advisor: One Big Beautiful Bill Act changes 1099 thresholds
- Avalara: OBBBA 1099 reporting threshold

## Frequently asked questions
When are 1065 and 1120-S returns due in 2027?
Monday 15 March 2027 for calendar-year partnerships and S corporations, with K-1s. Form 7004 extends the filing date to 15 September 2027.

When is the 2027 tax filing deadline for individuals?
Thursday 15 April 2027 for 2026 Form 1040 returns. Form 4868 extends filing, but not payment, to 15 October 2027.

When are W-2s and 1099-NEC forms due in 2027?
Monday 1 February 2027, because 31 January 2027 falls on a Sunday. Both go to recipients and to the IRS or SSA by that date.

What is the 1099-NEC threshold for 2026 payments?
$2,000. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act raised the reporting threshold for Forms 1099-NEC and 1099-MISC from $600 to $2,000 for payments made in 2026, with inflation adjustments from 2027.

# Outsourced accounting and tax prep for CPA firms

US accounting and CPA firms use our Chartered Accountant-led team in India as an extension of their own: tax-return preparation support, bookkeeping, close and workpapers, prepared to your standards and reviewed by you before anything reaches your clients.

## What we prepare for US CPA firms

Work | What we prepare | What stays with you | 

Individual returns (Form 1040 and schedules) | Data entry from source documents, workpapers, draft return and an open-items list | Review, signature as paid preparer, e-file under your EFIN | 

Business returns (Forms 1065, 1120-S, 1120) | Trial balance to return, book-to-tax workpapers, draft K-1s | Review, signature and filing |

For calendar-year clients, partnership and S-corporation returns are due on 15 March and individual and C-corporation returns on 15 April, with extensions to 15 September and 15 October. We add capacity for those peaks so your team spends its time reviewing, not keying in data.

UK practice? See outsourced accounting for UK accountancy practices.

## The compliance questions US firms ask first

- Section 7216 consent. Before tax return information goes to a preparer outside the United States, the taxpayer must sign a consent in the form set by Rev. Proc. 2013-14, which includes a statement that the recipient is outside the US. We give you a checklist; the consent is between you and your client.

- Social Security numbers. A full SSN can go offshore only if the consent covers it and both firms maintain an adequate data protection safeguard. Otherwise SSNs are masked before files reach us.

- PTINs. Anyone who prepares or helps prepare federal returns for compensation needs a PTIN, so we arrange PTINs for the staff assigned to your returns before any tax-prep work starts.

- Your EFIN and signature. We never sign or e-file. Your licensed preparer reviews, signs and files.

- Your security plan. Tax preparers must keep a written information security plan. We work inside yours: your remote desktop or portal, with multi-factor logins you create and can revoke, so client files stay in your environment.

## Frequently asked questions
Can a US CPA firm outsource tax return preparation to India?
Yes. It is legal and common, provided the firm gets each taxpayer's Section 7216 consent before return information goes outside the US, masks SSNs unless the consent and safeguards allow them, and keeps review, signature and e-filing in the US firm. Offshore staff who help prepare returns need PTINs.

Which returns can you prepare for a CPA firm?
We prepare Form 1040 individual returns and Forms 1065, 1120-S and 1120 business returns as drafts with workpapers, for your licensed preparer to review, sign and file. We also handle bookkeeping, monthly close, 1099 listings and audit workpapers.

Do your staff need a PTIN to work on US returns?
Yes. The IRS requires anyone who prepares or assists in preparing federal tax returns for compensation to have a PTIN, including preparers outside the US. We arrange PTINs for the staff assigned to your returns before any tax-prep work starts.

How do you protect client data?
We sign confidentiality and data-processing agreements before access, work inside your systems through logins you control and can revoke, and can work entirely inside your systems so client files stay with you. You decide what we can see.

How much does outsourced accounting from India cost?
It is quoted per return or as a fixed monthly fee once we see your volumes and return types, and is usually well below the cost of a local hire. Start with a pilot on a few files to judge quality first.

Do you work with UK, Canadian and Australian firms?
Yes. UK practices use us for bookkeeping, VAT, year-end accounts, CT600 and SA100 preparation and MTD quarterly updates; see our page for UK accountancy practices.

## MTD for Income Tax has added four deadlines a year

From 6 April 2026, sole traders and landlords with qualifying income (gross, not profit) over £50,000 must keep digital records and send quarterly updates; the threshold falls to £30,000 from April 2027 and £20,000 from April 2028. Updates are due on 7 August, 7 November, 7 February and 7 May. That is more work per client, all year round, which is where an offshore team helps most. # Clean books every month, ready for your accountant

Small businesses and founders in the US and UK use our Chartered Accountant-led team to keep their books up to date: transactions coded, accounts reconciled and a clear monthly report, so year-end and tax time are quick and cheaper.

Get a bookkeeping quote
hello@durgeshchavda.com

## What you get each month

For CPA firms

# Outsourcing tax preparation to India: 7216 consent, PTINs and data security

Offshore tax preparation is legal and widely used by US firms, but a few rules decide whether you are compliant. Here is what has to be in place before a single return leaves your office.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 1 November 2026·5 min read

Talk to us about a pilot
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- Get Section 7216 consent (Rev. Proc. 2013-14 format) before return information goes outside the US.
- Send SSNs only with consent plus an adequate data protection safeguard on both sides; otherwise mask them.
- Offshore preparers need PTINs; review, signature and e-file stay with the US firm.

## 1. Section 7216: get the client’s consent first

Section 7216 of the Internal Revenue Code makes it an offence for a return preparer to disclose tax return information without permission. Disclosing to another preparer outside the United States, even one in your own group, needs the taxpayer’s prior written consent (Treas. Reg. 301.7216-3).

- For Form 1040 clients, the consent must follow the format in Rev. Proc. 2013-14, including the mandatory statements and the statement that the recipient is outside the US.

- The consent must be signed before the disclosure. If it states no duration, it lasts one year from signing.

- Build the consent into your engagement letter process so it is collected at onboarding, not in March.

## 2. Social Security numbers need a safeguard

Under Rev. Proc. 2013-14, a taxpayer can consent to their SSN going to a preparer outside the US only if both the US preparer and the offshore preparer maintain an adequate data protection safeguard, and the US preparer verifies it. Without that, mask SSNs before files are shared.

## 3. PTINs for offshore staff

Anyone who prepares or helps prepare federal tax returns for compensation must have a Preparer Tax Identification Number. That includes preparers outside the US; those without an SSN apply with Form W-12 together with Form 8946.

## 4. Security: your plan covers the offshore team

- Tax preparers must keep a written information security plan under the FTC Safeguards Rule (see IRS Publication 5708).

- Give offshore staff access through your remote desktop or portal, with multi-factor authentication and accounts you can disable.

- Keep files off local machines, block downloads and USB storage, and log access.

- Put confidentiality and data-processing terms in the contract, including breach notification.

## 5. Keep review, signature and e-file in the US

The offshore team prepares; your licensed preparer reviews, signs as paid preparer and files under your EFIN. That keeps professional responsibility where your clients and regulators expect it.

## Checklist before you send the first file

- 7216 consent in the Rev. Proc. 2013-14 format, signed and on file
- SSN safeguard verified, or SSNs masked
- PTINs for every offshore preparer
- Security plan updated for offshore access
- Contract with confidentiality, data and breach terms
- Review and sign-off workflow in the US

Looking for a team that works this way? See outsourced accounting and tax prep for CPA firms.

## Sources

- IRS: Rev. Proc. 2013-14
- IRS: Section 7216 frequently asked questions
- IRS: PTIN requirements for tax return preparers
- The CPA Journal: considerations for tax return preparers outsourcing overseas (Aug 2025)
Planning the season? US tax deadlines 2027: the busy-season calendar.
Comparing providers? 12 questions to ask an offshore accounting partner.

## Frequently asked questions
Is it legal for a CPA firm to outsource tax returns to India?
Yes, if the firm gets each taxpayer's prior written consent under Section 7216 before disclosing return information to a preparer outside the US, follows Rev. Proc. 2013-14 for Form 1040 clients, and protects SSNs with an adequate data protection safeguard or masks them.

Does a client have to consent to offshore tax preparation?
Yes. Treas. Reg. 301.7216-3 requires the taxpayer's prior written consent before tax return information is disclosed to a preparer located outside the United States, even within the same firm.

Can an SSN be sent to an offshore tax preparer?
Only if the taxpayer's consent covers it and both the US preparer and the offshore preparer maintain an adequate data protection safeguard verified by the US preparer, under Rev. Proc. 2013-14. Otherwise mask the SSN.

Do offshore tax preparers need a PTIN?
Yes. Anyone who prepares or assists in preparing federal tax returns for compensation needs a PTIN, wherever they are located. Preparers without an SSN apply using Form W-12 with Form 8946.

# MTD for Income Tax: the 7 November 2026 quarterly update

Making Tax Digital for Income Tax started on 6 April 2026. The first quarterly update was due on 7 August; the second, covering 6 July to 5 October, is due on 7 November 2026. Here is what sole traders, landlords and their accountants need to know.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 1 November 2026·4 min read

Get help with MTD updates
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- Next MTD for Income Tax quarterly update: 7 November 2026 (6 July to 5 October 2026).
- In from April 2026 if qualifying income over £50,000; £30,000 from 2027 and £20,000 from 2028.
- No penalty points for late quarterly updates in the first 12 months; late returns still penalised.

Next deadline: 7 November 2026, for the quarter 6 July to 5 October 2026 (standard quarters). If you elected calendar quarters, check the period dates in your software.

## Who has to send quarterly updates

From | Qualifying income over | Based on | 

6 April 2026 | £50,000 | 2024-25 tax return | 

6 April 2027 | £30,000 | 2025-26 tax return | 

6 April 2028 | £20,000 | 2026-27 tax return | 

Qualifying income is gross self-employment and property income, not profit. Employment income and dividends do not count towards the threshold.

## Deadlines for 2026-27

Quarter (standard) | Update due | 

6 April to 5 July 2026 | 7 August 2026 | 

6 July to 5 October 2026 | 7 November 2026 | 

6 October 2026 to 5 January 2027 | 7 February 2027 | 

6 January to 5 April 2027 | 7 May 2027 | 

After the year ends, the tax return (final declaration) for 2026-27 is due by 31 January 2028.

## What goes in a quarterly update

- Totals of income and expenses by category, sent from MTD-compatible software built on the digital records you keep.

- A separate update for each business: each sole trade, UK property and foreign property income.

- No tax is paid with a quarterly update; payment dates are unchanged.

## Penalties

For people who had to start on 6 April 2026, HMRC has said it will not apply penalty points for late quarterly updates in the first 12 months. Penalty points still apply to late tax returns, so do not treat the first year as optional.

## For accountants: four extra deadlines per client

MTD turns an annual job into a quarterly one. Practices that keep up usually move clients to monthly bookkeeping in the software, so each quarterly update is a review, not a scramble. That categorising and reconciling is work an offshore team does well, leaving you to review and submit as agent. See outsourced accounting for UK practices.

## Sources

- GOV.UK: Send quarterly updates (Making Tax Digital for Income Tax)
- GOV.UK: Deadline approaches for first Making Tax Digital quarterly update
- ATT: How does the income exemption work for MTD?
Next big date: self assessment deadline, 31 January 2027.

## Frequently asked questions
When is the next MTD for Income Tax quarterly update due?
7 November 2026, for the standard quarter 6 July to 5 October 2026. The following updates are due on 7 February 2027 and 7 May 2027.

Who has to use MTD for Income Tax from April 2026?
Sole traders and landlords whose qualifying income, meaning gross self-employment and property income, was over £50,000 in 2024-25. The threshold falls to £30,000 from April 2027 and £20,000 from April 2028.

Is there a penalty for a late MTD quarterly update?
For people mandated from 6 April 2026, HMRC has said it will not apply penalty points for late quarterly updates in the first 12 months. Penalty points still apply to late tax returns.

Do I pay tax with each quarterly update?
No. Quarterly updates only report income and expenses; tax is still paid on the usual self assessment dates.

Markets · Diwali

# Muhurat trading 2026: date, time and how your Diwali trades are taxed

The stock exchanges open for a special one-hour Diwali session on Sunday, 8 November 2026. Many investors place a token trade for luck. Here is when the session runs and, just as important, how each kind of trade is taxed.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 15 October 2026·4 min read

Ask about your trading tax
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Booked a gain this year? Get your capital gains and income tax return handled by a Chartered Accountant. Ask on WhatsApp (first 10 messages free) or book a 30-minute call for ₹499.Ask on WhatsAppBook a call

Key takeaways
- Muhurat trading: Sunday 8 November 2026, from about 2:20 pm.
- Intraday = speculative income; delivery = 20% STCG or 12.5% LTCG above ₹1.25 lakh; F&O = business income.
- No special Diwali tax benefit; gifts of shares to relatives are not taxed.

Date and time: Sunday, 8 November 2026 (Diwali, Laxmi Pujan). The main equity session starts at about 2:20 pm IST after a pre-open from about 2:05 pm, per the exchanges’ circulars of 19 October as reported by brokers. Closing times differ between reports, so check the NSE or BSE circular before you trade.

## How Muhurat trades are taxed

Type of trade | How it is taxed | Watch out | 

Intraday (bought and sold the same day, no delivery) | Speculative business income, taxed at your slab rate | Speculative losses can be set off only against speculative income; carry forward 4 years | 

Delivery purchase, sold within 12 months | Short-term capital gain at 20% plus cess | The 12 months start from the purchase date (8 November) | 

Delivery purchase, sold after 12 months | 12.5% on long-term gains above ₹1.25 lakh a year | The ₹1.25 lakh exemption is shared across listed shares and equity funds | 

Futures and options | Non-speculative business income at your slab rate | Reported in ITR-3; turnover can trigger a tax audit | 

Muhurat trades are ordinary trades for tax: there is no special Diwali rate or exemption, and securities transaction tax applies as usual.

## Gifting shares on Diwali

- Shares gifted by a relative are not taxed in the hands of the person receiving them.

- Gifts from friends and others are taxable income if their total value in the year exceeds ₹50,000.

- When the gift is later sold, the giver’s purchase price and holding period carry over.

## Work out your tax

Use the free IPO and listed-share tax calculator for short- and long-term gains, or the gold tax calculator if you are buying gold for Dhanteras on 6 November. NRIs trading through PIS accounts pay the same rates, with tax deducted by the broker: see NRIs and Indian shares.

## Sources

- Bajaj Broking — Muhurat trading 2026 date and timings
- NSE India — circulars

## Frequently asked questions
When is Muhurat trading in 2026?
On Sunday, 8 November 2026, for Diwali. The main equity session starts at about 2:20 pm IST after a pre-open from about 2:05 pm, as reported from the exchanges' circulars; check NSE or BSE for the exact closing time.

How is Muhurat trading profit taxed?
Like any other trade. Intraday profit is speculative business income at your slab rate; shares bought for delivery and sold within 12 months are taxed at 20% as short-term capital gains, and after 12 months at 12.5% above ₹1.25 lakh a year; F&O profit is business income.

Is there any tax benefit for Muhurat trading?
No. There is no special rate or exemption for trades in the Diwali session; securities transaction tax and the normal rules apply.

Is gifting shares on Diwali taxable?
Not if the shares go to a relative. Gifts from non-relatives are taxable for the recipient if their total value in the year exceeds ₹50,000.

## How IPO gains are taxed (FY 2026-27)

When you sell | Tax | Notes | 

Within 12 months of allotment (including listing day) | 20% short-term capital gains | Plus surcharge (capped at 15%) and 4% cess. Selling on listing day is a delivery sale, not intraday. | 

After 12 months | 12.5% on long-term gains above ₹1.25 lakh a year | The ₹1.25 lakh exemption is shared across all listed shares and equity funds. | 

- Cost: your allotment (issue) price. Brokerage on sale is deductible; securities transaction tax (STT) is not.

- Losses: a short-term loss can be set off against short- or long-term gains; a long-term loss only against long-term gains. Carry forward up to 8 years if you file on time.

- NRIs: the broker deducts tax at source on the gain. File an Indian return to claim back any excess. See NRIs in IPOs.

Worked examples and the full rules: tax on IPO listing gains in India.
Trading on Diwali? Muhurat trading 2026: date, time and tax.

## Frequently asked questions
How much tax do I pay on IPO profit in India?
If you sell within 12 months of allotment, the gain is short-term and taxed at 20% plus 4% cess (and surcharge if your income is above ₹50 lakh). After 12 months, gains above ₹1.25 lakh a year are taxed at 12.5% plus cess.

Is IPO listing gain taxable if I sell on listing day?
Yes. Shares allotted in an IPO and sold on listing day are a delivery sale, so the gain is a short-term capital gain taxed at 20% plus cess, not speculative income.

How much tax on Jio Platforms listing gains?
Jio Platforms listed at ₹1,358 against a ₹1,119 issue price. On a 12-share lot sold at the listing price, the gain is ₹2,868 and the tax is about ₹597 (20% plus 4% cess, before any surcharge).

Do NRIs pay tax on IPO gains in India?
Yes, at the same rates. The broker deducts the tax at source when the shares are sold; NRIs can file an Indian return to claim back any excess.

# Gold tax calculator: tax on selling gold in 2026

Selling old jewellery before Dhanteras (6 November 2026), or booking profit on gold ETFs? See the tax on your gain, then read the rules for buying, gifting and holding gold.

Ask about your gold tax
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Booked a gain this year? Get your capital gains and income tax return handled by a Chartered Accountant. Ask on WhatsApp (first 10 messages free) or book a 30-minute call for ₹499.Ask on WhatsAppBook a call

## How gold is taxed when you sell

Type of gold | Long-term after | Long-term tax | Short-term tax | 

Jewellery, coins, bars, digital gold | 24 months | 12.5%, no indexation | Your slab rate | 

Gold ETFs (listed) | 12 months | 12.5% | Your slab rate | 

Gold mutual funds (fund of funds) | 24 months | 12.5% | Your slab rate | 

Plus 4% cess, and surcharge if your income is above ₹50 lakh (capped at 15% on long-term gains). Keep the original bill: without it, proving your cost is hard.

## Buying gold this Dhanteras

- GST: 3% on the value of the gold, plus 5% on making charges.

- PAN: needed for jewellery purchases of ₹2 lakh or more.

- Cash: a jeweller cannot accept ₹2 lakh or more in cash from you for one purchase; pay by card, UPI or bank transfer.

- Exchanging old jewellery: swapping old gold for new is treated as selling the old piece, so a gain can arise.

## Gold as a gift

Gold received from relatives, or on your marriage, is not taxed. Gifts from friends and others are taxed as income if their total value in the year is above ₹50,000. When you later sell gifted or inherited gold, the original owner’s cost and holding period carry over to you.

## How much gold can you keep at home?

There is no legal limit on owning gold you can explain. Under CBDT Instruction No. 1916 (1994), during a tax search officers do not seize jewellery up to 500 g for a married woman, 250 g for an unmarried woman and 100 g for a man, even without documents. Above that, keep bills, gift records or inheritance papers.

NRIs bringing gold to India: customs rules apply. See NRI tax services. Selling property instead? Use the property capital gains calculator.
Trading on Diwali? Muhurat trading 2026: date, time and tax.

## Frequently asked questions
What is the tax on selling gold jewellery in 2026?
If you held it for more than 24 months, the gain is long-term and taxed at 12.5% without indexation, plus cess. If you held it for 24 months or less, the gain is added to your income and taxed at your slab rate.

Is there tax on gold ETF profit?
Yes. Gold ETFs held for more than 12 months are taxed at 12.5% on the gain; within 12 months the gain is taxed at your slab rate.

How much gold can I keep at home in India?
There is no legal limit if you can explain the source. Under CBDT Instruction 1916, officers do not seize up to 500 g for a married woman, 250 g for an unmarried woman and 100 g for a man during a search, even without documents.

Is gold received as a gift taxable?
Not if it comes from a relative or on your marriage. Gifts from others are taxable if their total value in the year exceeds ₹50,000.

Is PAN required to buy gold on Dhanteras?
Yes, for jewellery purchases of ₹2 lakh or more. Jewellers also cannot accept ₹2 lakh or more in cash for a purchase.

For companies outside India

# How to choose an advisor in India: a checklist for foreign companies

If you are setting up, buying from or investing in India, the right local advisor saves months, and the wrong one costs far more than their fee. Here is how to pick one: which kind of advisor you need, how to check them in ten minutes, and what to ask before you sign.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 15 October 2026·5 min read

Book a free 15-min call
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- Pick the right kind: advisory, practising CA (audits and certificates), company secretary, lawyer.
- Check ICAI/ICSI membership and the MCA record; ask who does the work and who signs.
- Avoid anyone who promises to 'settle' things with officials or won't give a written engagement letter.

## Which kind of advisor do you need?

What you need | Who does it | Note | 
Business and tax advisory, set-up, due diligence, CFO support | Consultancy and advisory firms (often led by Chartered Accountants) | Structure, filings plan, accounting, reporting, partner checks | 
Statutory audit, tax audit, transfer pricing report, Form 146 certificate | A chartered accountant in practice | These must be signed by a practising CA; ask who will sign | 
Company law filings and secretarial work | A company secretary (CS) | Board processes, registers and annual filings with the Registrar | 
Contracts, disputes, licences | A law firm | Shareholder agreements, JV and distribution contracts, litigation | 

Most foreign companies need one advisor who coordinates the rest, rather than four separate firms that don’t talk to each other.

## Check them in ten minutes

- Professional membership: Chartered Accountants are members of ICAI, which has an online member search. Company secretaries are members of ICSI.

- The company behind them: look up the firm or company on the Ministry of Corporate Affairs master data: status, directors and filing history.

- Real work, real people: named team members with LinkedIn profiles, published guides, and at least one reference you can call.

- Presence where you need it: someone who can actually visit your site, supplier or partner.

## Seven questions to ask before you sign

- Who exactly will do the work, and who is my day-to-day contact?
- Can you show work you have done for companies from my country?
- Will I get reports in English, on my head office’s calendar?
- Is the fee fixed, and what is outside the scope?
- Who signs the audits and certificates, if you don’t?
- How do you handle my data and documents?
- How quickly do you reply, and in which time zone?

## Red flags

- Promises to “guarantee” approvals or “settle” matters with officials. Under your own country’s anti-bribery law this is a risk to you, not just to them.

- No written engagement letter, or fees asked in cash.

- Vague answers on who signs audits and certificates.

- No one available in your working hours.

We handle set-up, FEMA/RBI reporting, accounting and reporting, tax and transfer pricing advisory, and due diligence for foreign companies, and coordinate the specialists you need. ## Sources

- Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI)
- Ministry of Corporate Affairs: company master data

## Frequently asked questions
How do I find a good business advisor in India as a foreign company?
Decide which kind of advisor you need (advisory, practising CA for audits and certificates, company secretary, lawyer), check their professional membership and company record online, ask who will do the work and who signs, insist on a written fixed-scope engagement and English reporting, and take a reference from a client in your country.

Who can sign a transfer pricing report in India?
The accountant's report on international transactions must be signed by a chartered accountant in practice. If your advisor is a consultancy rather than a practising firm, ask who will sign it.

How do I check if an Indian Chartered Accountant is genuine?
Use ICAI's online member search to confirm membership, and check any firm or company they run on the Ministry of Corporate Affairs master data.

Can I talk to an advisor in India before deciding?
Yes. CA Durgesh Chavda offers a free 15-minute call for companies outside India, with slots shown in your own time zone.
