Japan · Tax

# Paying your Japanese parent from India: withholding tax and the 10% treaty rate

When an Indian subsidiary pays dividends, royalties, technical fees or interest to its parent in Japan, India deducts tax at source. The India–Japan tax treaty caps that tax at 10%, against about 20% under Indian law, but only if the paperwork is in place before the payment.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 15 October 2026·5 min read

Get the treaty rate right
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Paying or getting paid across borders? We file Form 41 for foreign vendors, TDS returns (Forms 140 and 144) and remittance forms (145/146) for Indian payers, and set up treaty rates correctly.Free 15-min callWhatsApp

Key takeaways
- India–Japan treaty: 10% cap on dividends, interest, royalties and technical fees (domestic about 20%).
- Get the TRC and Form 41 before paying; remit with Forms 145/146.
- GST under reverse charge on imported services; transfer pricing on every related-party payment.

## Rates at a glance

Payment to Japan | Indian domestic rate | India–Japan treaty cap | Watch out | 
Dividends | 20% plus surcharge and cess | 10% | Board-declared dividend; Form 41 and TRC before payment | 
Interest on loans from the parent | 20% plus surcharge and cess (lower rates for some approved borrowings) | 10% | Loans from Japan are external commercial borrowings: check ECB rules first | 
Royalties (brand, technology licences) | 20% plus surcharge and cess | 10% | Royalty must be at arm’s length: transfer pricing applies | 
Fees for technical services | 20% plus surcharge and cess | 10% | Group service charges: keep evidence the services were actually rendered | 

The rate actually applied is the lower of the domestic rate and the treaty rate, provided the Japanese recipient is the beneficial owner and the documents below are in place.

## The paperwork, before you pay

- Tax residency certificate from the Japanese tax authorities for the parent company.

- Form 41 (the declaration that replaced Form 10F from 1 April 2026), with the parent’s details. See Form 41 and the no-PE declaration.

- A no permanent establishment declaration where relevant, so the payment is not treated as business income of a Japanese office in India.

- Form 145 online and, where required, a chartered accountant’s certificate in Form 146 (the old 15CA and 15CB) for the bank to remit.

## GST on royalties and service fees

When the Indian company imports services from Japan (technology licences, group management services, engineering support), GST is usually paid by the Indian company itself under reverse charge, and can normally be claimed back as input-tax credit if the company makes taxable supplies.

## Transfer pricing

Royalties, service fees and interest paid to the parent are related-party transactions. They need to be priced at arm’s length and documented every year, or the deduction in India can be cut in an assessment. For new Japanese subsidiaries, set the transfer pricing policy before the first invoice.

## How we help

We set up the treaty paperwork, review the agreements behind the payments, handle the remittance forms with the bank, and keep transfer pricing documentation in order, reporting to Japan in English. See India advisory for Japanese companies and India tax for foreign companies. 日本語: 日本語の概要.

## Sources

- Embassy of Japan in India — Protocol amending the India–Japan tax convention
- Income Tax Department — Notification 1136/2006 (India–Japan protocol)

## Frequently asked questions
What is the withholding tax on royalties paid from India to Japan?
Under the India–Japan tax treaty, Indian tax on royalties paid to a Japanese beneficial owner is capped at 10% of the gross amount, provided the recipient gives a Japanese tax residency certificate and Form 41. Otherwise the domestic rate of 20% plus surcharge and cess applies.

Is the treaty rate on dividends from India to Japan 10%?
Yes. The India–Japan treaty, as amended by the 2006 protocol, caps Indian tax on dividends paid to a Japanese resident at 10%.

Which forms are needed to remit money from India to Japan in 2026?
From 1 April 2026 the bank needs Form 145 (formerly 15CA) and, for larger taxable payments, a chartered accountant's certificate in Form 146 (formerly 15CB); the treaty rate also needs a tax residency certificate and Form 41.

Please note: this guide is general information based on the rules as they stood on the review date above. Regulations and RBI/CBDT procedures change often — please get advice on your specific facts before acting.

Due diligence in India

# Due diligence in India for Canadian companies

Canadian firms are opening bases in India, buying from Indian suppliers and investing in Indian businesses. Before you sign with an Indian partner, supplier or target, we check them on the ground and report in English, working across Canadian time zones.

Discuss your Indian partner
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- CFPOA: no facilitation-payments exception since October 2017; a books-and-records offence since 2013.
- S-211: annual forced and child labour supply-chain reports due 31 May.
- Documented checks on Indian agents and suppliers support both.

## Why companies from here use us

- Canadian technology, services and resources companies keep adding Indian teams, suppliers and partners.

- Canadian boards and lenders expect documented, verifiable findings on foreign counterparties.

- India is 9.5 to 12.5 hours ahead of Canada, so we work Indian evenings for calls with Toronto and Vancouver.

## Your home-country rules — and what they mean for an Indian partner

- Corruption of Foreign Public Officials Act (CFPOA): Canada’s foreign bribery law since 1998. Amendments in 2013 added a books-and-records offence and nationality jurisdiction, and the exception for facilitation payments was repealed in October 2017, so small “speed” payments to Indian officials are not protected.

- Supply-chain reporting (S-211): since 1 January 2024, entities that meet the size thresholds report each year by 31 May on the steps they take to prevent and reduce forced labour and child labour in their supply chains. Indian suppliers are often part of that picture.

- What that means in India: documented checks on Indian agents, distributors, customs brokers and suppliers: who owns them, whether they deal with government bodies, how they are paid, and how they employ people. See supplier verification and India’s own anti-bribery law.

## The India side

- Trade deal: India–Canada CEPA talks are in progress; the fifth round was held in Ottawa on 5–9 October 2026, and both sides aim to conclude by the end of 2026.

- India–Canada tax treaty: Indian tax on interest is capped at 15%; dividends at 15% or 25%. See India advisory for clients in Canada.

- Setting up in India: the resident director rule · India entry · start small with an India Company Check (USD 249).

- Planning India? Book a free 15-minute call.

## What we check for you in India

- Identity, registrations and filed financial statements of the Indian partner — how it works.

- Financial, tax and FEMA review; related parties; litigation through public records and counsel.

- Promoters, directors, government links and how intermediaries are paid — for your anti-bribery and supply-chain files.

- Premises visits from Ahmedabad, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Rajkot or Dubai, with a written report in English.

- Full scope: partner due diligence · investment due diligence · supplier verification.

We are Chartered Accountants, not lawyers: home-country legal advice on compliance programmes stays with your counsel. Our reports are built to slot into their files.

## Sources

- Justice Laws — Corruption of Foreign Public Officials Act
- Public Safety Canada — Forced labour and child labour in supply chains

## Frequently asked questions
Who can do due diligence on an Indian company for a Canadian company?
CA Durgesh Chavda's team checks Indian partners, suppliers and targets for Canadian companies: records, financials, tax, FEMA, ownership, promoters and premises. Reports are in English, and calls run in Canadian business hours.

Does Canada's CFPOA allow facilitation payments in India?
No. The facilitation-payments exception in Canada's Corruption of Foreign Public Officials Act was repealed in October 2017, so small payments to speed up routine actions by Indian officials are not protected.

Does Canada's supply-chain law cover Indian suppliers?
It can. Entities reporting under the Fighting Against Forced Labour and Child Labour in Supply Chains Act describe, by 31 May each year, the steps they take to reduce forced and child labour risk across their supply chains, including suppliers in India.

India entry

# Resident director in India — the 182-day rule for foreign-owned companies

It is the question foreign founders ask most when setting up in India: do we need an Indian director? You don’t need an Indian partner, but you do need one director who lives in India for most of the year. Here is how the rule works and how foreign groups fill the seat safely.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 15 October 2026·5 min read

Get the structure right
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- Every Indian company needs one director who stays in India 182+ days in the financial year.
- Nationality doesn't matter; the other directors can live abroad.
- Limit authority, agree indemnity and keep filings current — 3 years of missed filings disqualifies directors for 5 years.

## The rule

- Two directors minimum for a private limited company (Companies Act 2013, section 149(1)). A public company needs three.

- At least one resident director — someone who stays in India for a total of 182 days or more in the financial year (section 149(3)). For a company incorporated during the year, the requirement applies proportionately.

- Nationality does not matter. A foreign national living in India can be the resident director; an Indian citizen living abroad usually cannot.

- The other director(s) can be anywhere in the world — typically executives of the foreign parent.

## Who can fill the seat

Option | Why it works | Watch out | 
An Indian employee (country manager, finance head) | Already in India; knows the business | Becomes a statutory officer; needs board-approved limits on authority | 
A director relocating from the parent | Full control stays with the group | Needs an employment visa and must actually spend 182 days in India | 
An NRI or Indian citizen in the group | Trusted, often easier visa position | Counts only if they spend 182 days in India in the financial year | 
An independent professional director | Fast; experienced in compliance | Check them carefully; agree indemnity, scope and fees in writing | 

## What the resident director is responsible for

A director is not a name on a form. Under section 166 they owe duties of good faith, care and diligence, and they can be treated as an “officer in default” for compliance failures they knew about. The biggest practical risk: if the company fails to file its financial statements or annual returns for three continuous financial years, every director is disqualified for five years from being appointed to any Indian company (section 164(2)). A director can also hold at most 20 directorships (10 public companies).

## Protecting both sides

- Board-approved limits: the resident director signs statutory filings; banking and contract authority stays with the parent’s nominees or needs dual signatures.

- Reserved matters in the articles or shareholder resolutions: borrowing, new bank accounts, related-party deals, hiring above a level.

- Indemnity and D&O insurance for the director, and a written engagement setting scope and fees.

- A compliance calendar someone owns — most director problems start with missed AOC-4, MGT-7 or tax filings. See Indian subsidiary compliance.

- Background checks on any independent director: other directorships, disqualifications, litigation — the same checks we run for partner due diligence.

## Paperwork

- Each director needs a Director Identification Number (DIN) and a digital signature certificate. At incorporation, DINs for up to three directors are allotted through the SPICe+ form.

- Foreign directors’ passports and address proofs must be notarised and apostilled (or consularised) — usually the slowest step.

- Directors appointed later are reported to the Registrar on Form DIR-12 within 30 days.

- A foreign director who comes to India to work for the company needs an employment visa; a business visa generally covers board meetings and short visits.

Not sure how to structure it? Book a free 15-minute call or compare entity types with the structure chooser.

## Sources

- Companies Act 2013 — India Code
- Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA21)

## Frequently asked questions
Does a foreign-owned company in India need an Indian director?
It needs a resident director, not an Indian one: at least one director must stay in India for 182 days or more in the financial year. Nationality does not matter, and the other directors can live abroad.

Can an NRI be the resident director of an Indian company?
Only if they actually spend at least 182 days in India during the financial year. An Indian citizen living abroad for most of the year does not meet the rule.

What happens if a company does not have a resident director?
It is in breach of section 149(3) of the Companies Act 2013. Fix it by appointing a director who meets the 182-day test and filing DIR-12 within 30 days.

What is the biggest risk for a resident director?
Disqualification: if the company fails to file financial statements or annual returns for three continuous financial years, its directors are disqualified for five years from other Indian directorships.

Please note: this guide is general information based on the rules as they stood on the review date above. Regulations and RBI/CBDT procedures change often — please get advice on your specific facts before acting.

# Planning to operate in India? Talk to Durgesh — 15 minutes, free.

Whether you’re setting up a subsidiary, appointing a distributor, sourcing, investing or hiring in India, a short call saves weeks of guesswork. Book a free 15-minute intro in your own time zone — or start with the quick answers below.

## How the call works

- In 15 minutes you get the right structure, the main approvals and filings, realistic timelines, and what it would cost us to do it — no obligation.

## What we can cover

- Entering India: subsidiary vs LLP vs branch or liaison office, FDI rules, set-up steps — India entry · structure chooser.

- Partners and suppliers: due diligence before you sign or pay — partner due diligence · India Company Check (USD 249).

- Investing or acquiring: transaction due diligence, valuation and FEMA.

- Running the Indian entity: accounting, GST, payroll, transfer pricing, reporting to you — subsidiary compliance.

- Problems: tax notices, suspected fraud — tax notices · forensic audit.

## Quick answers to what foreigners ask most

### Can a foreigner own 100% of a company in India?
Yes, in most sectors, under the automatic route — no prior government approval. A few sectors have caps or need approval, and investors from countries sharing a land border with India need approval (with a relaxation for non-controlling stakes up to 10%).

### Do I need an Indian partner or director?
You don't need an Indian partner, but a private company needs at least two directors, and at least one director must have stayed in India for 182 days or more in the financial year. Many foreign companies use an Indian employee or a professional resident director.

### Is there a minimum capital requirement?
No minimum paid-up capital for a private limited company. Capital should match the plan, and foreign investment must be reported to the RBI (Form FC-GPR within 30 days of issuing shares).

### How long does it take to set up a company in India?
Usually a few weeks once documents are ready. Foreign shareholder and director documents must be notarised and apostilled (or consularised), which often takes longer than the Indian filing itself.

### Subsidiary, LLP, branch or liaison office?
A subsidiary (private limited company) suits most businesses. An LLP can take FDI only in sectors with 100% automatic-route FDI and no FDI-linked conditions. Branch, liaison and project offices need approval through an authorised bank and are taxed differently.

### What tax will my Indian company pay?
A domestic company can opt for a 22% base rate (about 25.17% with surcharge and cess). Dividends to the foreign parent are taxed in India, often at a reduced treaty rate with a tax residency certificate and Form 41.

### Can I hire in India without setting up a company?
Yes, through an employer of record or contractors, but watch permanent-establishment risk. See hiring in India without an entity.

### How do I check an Indian partner or supplier?
Start with public records — company filings, GST, directors, charges and courts — then visit. A fixed-fee India Company Check costs USD 249.

### What visa do I need?
A business visa usually covers meetings and setting up; working in India for an Indian entity generally needs an employment visa. Check the current rules for your nationality.

### Can I talk to someone before deciding?
Yes — book a free 15-minute call. Topmate shows available slots in your own time zone.

NRI tax · Canada

# NRIs in Canada — Indian tax and Canadian tax, side by side

Canada is home to one of the largest Indian diasporas. If you live there and still have income or assets in India, India taxes your Indian income and Canada taxes your worldwide income — and wants your Indian assets reported. Here is how to keep both sides clean.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 15 October 2026·5 min read

Sort your Indian tax
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Hold anything abroad? FAST-DS 2026 closes on 31 December: a one-time chance to declare foreign accounts, RSUs and assets missed in your returns, from a flat ₹1 lakh. Check what you would pay or get it filed.

Quick reference: NRI income tax slab 2026-27 (no ₹12 lakh rebate, refund example).
Key takeaways
- NRE interest is exempt in India but taxable in Canada.
- File T1135 if Indian investments cost more than CAD 100,000 at any time in the year.
- Use a CRA residency certificate + Form 41 for the 15% treaty rate on interest; claim the foreign tax credit in Canada.

## Income by income: India vs Canada

Income or asset | India | Canada (residents) | Watch out | 
NRO interest | Taxed; bank deducts TDS (30% plus surcharge and cess by default) | Taxable; claim the foreign tax credit | Treaty caps Indian tax at 15% with a Canadian residency certificate and Form 41 | 
NRE / FCNR interest | Exempt while you are an NRI | Taxable for Canadian residents | Often missed on Canadian returns | 
Dividends from Indian shares | Taxed in India; treaty cap 15% (company with 10%+ voting power) or 25% | Taxable; credit for Indian tax | Claim the treaty rate | 
Sale of Indian property | Capital gains tax; buyer deducts TDS | Taxable as a capital gain; credit for Indian tax | Lower-TDS certificate (Form 128) avoids over-deduction | 
Indian bank accounts, shares, funds, property held for investment | — | Report on Form T1135 if total cost exceeds CAD 100,000 at any time in the year | Penalties for late or missing T1135 | 
Rent from Indian property | Taxed; tenant may deduct TDS | Taxable; credit for Indian tax | File an Indian return to claim deductions | 

## Form T1135: reporting Indian assets

Canadian residents must file Form T1135 (Foreign Income Verification Statement) if the total cost of their specified foreign property — Indian bank deposits, shares, mutual funds and property held for investment — exceeds CAD 100,000 at any time in the year. A home you use personally is generally not included. Late or missing filings attract penalties, so keep a running cost record of Indian assets.

## Avoiding double tax

- In India: claim the India–Canada treaty rate (for example 15% on interest) with a certificate of residency from the Canada Revenue Agency and Form 41.

- In Canada: claim the foreign tax credit for Indian tax paid on the same income.

- File an Indian return to recover excess TDS — see NRI income tax return.

## Moving to or from Canada

Your Indian residential status depends on days spent in India — see residential status and RNOR. Planning a move back? Read returning to India — most of the RNOR planning applies to Canada too.

## How we help

We handle the Indian side — returns, TDS refunds, lower-TDS certificates, property sales and repatriation up to USD 1 million a year — and coordinate with your Canadian accountant. See NRI tax services and India advisory for clients in Canada.

## Sources

- Canada Revenue Agency — Form T1135, Foreign Income Verification Statement
Sending money between India and your country? Limits, forms and local tax rules.

## Frequently asked questions
Is NRE interest taxable in Canada?
Yes. NRE interest is exempt in India while you are an NRI, but Canada taxes its residents on worldwide income, so it must be reported on your Canadian return.

Do I need to file T1135 for my Indian bank accounts?
Yes, if the total cost of your specified foreign property — including Indian bank deposits, shares, mutual funds and investment property — exceeds CAD 100,000 at any time in the year.

What is the treaty rate on Indian interest for Canadian residents?
The India–Canada tax treaty caps Indian tax on interest at 15%, available with a Canadian certificate of residency and Form 41; otherwise the bank deducts 30% plus surcharge and cess on NRO interest.

NRI tax · UK

# NRIs in the UK — Indian tax and UK tax, side by side

If you live in the UK and have income or assets in India, both countries may tax it. India taxes your Indian income; the UK taxes its residents on worldwide income. Here is how the two fit together — and where people slip.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 15 October 2026·6 min read

Sort your Indian tax
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Hold anything abroad? FAST-DS 2026 closes on 31 December: a one-time chance to declare foreign accounts, RSUs and assets missed in your returns, from a flat ₹1 lakh. Check what you would pay or get it filed.

Quick reference: NRI income tax slab 2026-27 (no ₹12 lakh rebate, refund example).
Key takeaways
- NRE interest is exempt in India but generally taxable in the UK.
- Indian mutual funds can fall under UK offshore fund rules — gains taxed as income.
- Use an HMRC certificate of residence + Form 41 for treaty rates; claim foreign tax credit relief in the UK.

## Income by income: India vs the UK

Income or asset | India | UK (residents) | Watch out | 
NRO interest | Taxed; bank deducts TDS (30% plus surcharge and cess by default) | Taxable for UK residents; foreign tax credit relief | Treaty reduces Indian tax with an HMRC certificate of residence and Form 41 | 
NRE / FCNR interest | Exempt while you are an NRI | Taxable for UK residents (unless covered by the FIG regime) | Often missed on UK returns | 
Dividends from Indian shares | Taxed in India; treaty caps it at 10% in most cases | Taxable; credit for Indian tax | Claim the treaty rate rather than the 20% domestic rate | 
Sale of Indian property | Capital gains tax; buyer deducts TDS | Taxable for UK residents; credit for Indian tax | Lower-TDS certificate (Form 128) avoids over-deduction | 
Indian mutual funds | Capital gains tax in India | Offshore fund rules — gains on non-reporting funds taxed as income | Check reporting-fund status before investing | 
Rent from Indian property | Taxed; tenant may deduct TDS | Taxable; credit for Indian tax | File an Indian return to claim deductions | 

## The UK’s FIG regime (from April 2025)

From 6 April 2025 the UK replaced the old remittance basis for non-domiciled residents with a four-year foreign income and gains (FIG) regime for people arriving after ten years of non-residence. Within those four years, qualifying foreign income and gains can be exempt from UK tax if claimed; after that, worldwide income is taxed. If you moved to the UK recently, check whether you qualify before reporting Indian income.

## Avoiding double tax

- In India: claim the India–UK treaty rate (for example a 10% cap on dividends in most cases) by giving the payer an HMRC certificate of residence and Form 41.

- In the UK: claim foreign tax credit relief for Indian tax paid on the same income on your Self Assessment return.

- File an Indian return to recover excess TDS — see NRI income tax return.

## Which country are you resident in?

India uses day counts (182 days, or 60 days plus 365 days over four years, with special rules for visiting NRIs) — see residential status and RNOR. The UK uses its Statutory Residence Test. You can be resident in both in a year; the treaty’s tie-breaker rules then decide where you are treated as resident for treaty purposes.

## How we help

We handle the Indian side — returns, TDS refunds, lower-TDS certificates, property sales and repatriation — and work with your UK accountant so both returns agree. See NRI tax services and India advisory for clients in the UK.

## Sources

- GOV.UK — Tax on foreign income
- GOV.UK — Get a certificate of residence
- GOV.UK — Offshore funds: list of reporting funds
Living in Canada? NRIs in Canada: Indian tax and Canadian tax.
Next big date: self assessment deadline, 31 January 2027.
Sending money between India and your country? Limits, forms and local tax rules.

## Frequently asked questions
Is NRE interest taxable in the UK?
Yes, for UK residents in general — NRE interest is exempt in India while you are an NRI, but the UK taxes residents on worldwide income. Recent arrivals may be able to claim relief under the UK's four-year foreign income and gains regime.

How are Indian mutual funds taxed for UK residents?
Under the UK's offshore fund rules, gains on funds without UK reporting-fund status are generally taxed as income rather than capital gains, so check a fund's status before investing.

How do NRIs in the UK claim India–UK treaty rates?
Give the Indian payer an HMRC certificate of residence and Form 41. For example, the treaty generally caps Indian tax on dividends at 10%.

What replaced the UK remittance basis?
From 6 April 2025, a four-year foreign income and gains (FIG) regime for people becoming UK resident after ten years of non-residence.

NRI tax · USA

# NRIs in the US — Indian tax and US reporting, side by side

If you live in the US and have money in India, two tax systems apply. India taxes your Indian income; the US taxes your worldwide income and wants your Indian accounts reported. Most problems come from the gaps between the two.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 15 October 2026·6 min read

Sort your Indian tax
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Hold anything abroad? FAST-DS 2026 closes on 31 December: a one-time chance to declare foreign accounts, RSUs and assets missed in your returns, from a flat ₹1 lakh. Check what you would pay or get it filed.

Quick reference: NRI income tax slab 2026-27 (no ₹12 lakh rebate, refund example).
Key takeaways
- NRE interest is exempt in India but taxable in the US.
- FBAR above USD 10,000 combined; FATCA Form 8938 above USD 50,000/75,000 (single, in the US).
- Indian mutual funds are generally PFICs — take US advice; use Form 6166 + Form 41 for treaty rates in India.

## Income by income: India vs the US

Income or asset | India | US (residents and citizens) | Watch out | 
NRO interest | Taxed; bank deducts TDS (30% plus surcharge and cess by default) | Taxable; claim credit for Indian tax | Treaty caps Indian tax at 15% with a US residency certificate (Form 6166) and Form 41 | 
NRE / FCNR interest | Exempt while you are an NRI | Taxable for US residents and citizens | Often missed on US returns | 
Rent from Indian property | Taxed; tenant may deduct TDS | Taxable; foreign tax credit for Indian tax | File an Indian return to claim deductions | 
Sale of Indian property | Capital gains tax; buyer deducts TDS on the sale | Taxable; foreign tax credit | Lower-TDS certificate (Form 128) avoids over-deduction | 
Indian mutual funds | Capital gains tax in India | Generally treated as PFICs — Form 8621, punitive default rules | Take US advice before buying or holding | 
Indian shares (direct) | Capital gains tax in India | Taxable; foreign tax credit | No PFIC issue for ordinary company shares | 

## US reporting of Indian accounts

- FBAR (FinCEN Form 114): required if your foreign financial accounts together exceed USD 10,000 at any time in the year. Due 15 April, with an automatic extension to 15 October.

- FATCA (Form 8938): filed with your US return when specified foreign assets exceed the thresholds — for a single filer living in the US, more than USD 50,000 on the last day of the year or USD 75,000 at any time (double for married filing jointly).

- PFIC (Form 8621): Indian mutual funds are generally passive foreign investment companies for US tax, with complex filings and potentially punitive tax.

## Avoiding double tax

- In India: claim the India–US treaty rate (for example 15% on interest) with a US tax residency certificate — Form 6166, requested from the IRS on Form 8802 — and Form 41. See the India–US DTAA guide.

- In the US: claim a foreign tax credit (Form 1116) for Indian tax paid on the same income.

- File an Indian return to get excess TDS refunded — see NRI income tax return.

## Moving money

NRO balances can be repatriated up to USD 1 million a year with Forms 145 and 146 — see NRO repatriation. Note the US 1% remittance tax on certain cash-funded transfers from the US.

## How we help

We handle the Indian side — returns, TDS refunds, lower-TDS certificates, property sales, repatriation — and coordinate with your US CPA so both returns tell the same story. US returns, FBAR and Form 8621 are signed by your US preparer. See NRI tax services and India advisory for clients in the US.

## Sources

- IRS — Report of Foreign Bank and Financial Accounts (FBAR)
- IRS — Comparison of Form 8938 and FBAR requirements
- IRS — Form 8802 (US residency certification, Form 6166)
Living in the UK? NRIs in the UK: Indian tax and UK tax.
Living in Canada? NRIs in Canada: Indian tax and Canadian tax.
Sending money between India and your country? Limits, forms and local tax rules.

## Frequently asked questions
Is NRE interest taxable in the US?
Yes, for US residents and citizens. NRE interest is exempt in India while you are an NRI, but the US taxes worldwide income, so it must be reported on your US return.

Do NRIs in the US need to file FBAR for Indian accounts?
Yes, if the combined balance of all foreign financial accounts exceeds USD 10,000 at any time in the year. FBAR (FinCEN Form 114) is due 15 April, with an automatic extension to 15 October.

Are Indian mutual funds a problem for US residents?
Generally yes. Indian mutual funds are usually treated as PFICs for US tax, which means Form 8621 filings and potentially punitive tax; take US advice before buying or holding them.

How do NRIs in the US claim India–US treaty rates?
Provide the Indian payer a US tax residency certificate (IRS Form 6166, requested on Form 8802) and Form 41. Interest is then capped at 15% (10% for bank loans) under the treaty.

US incorporation worldwide

# US company formation for non-residents — from anywhere in the world

Founders and companies outside the US form American LLCs and corporations to sell to US customers, raise from US investors or use US payment platforms. We set it up remotely and keep it compliant — whether you are in Dubai, London, Lagos, Singapore, São Paulo or Bengaluru.

Plan your US company
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Talk it through first — free. Book a 15-minute intro call with Durgesh to scope your requirement, timeline and fee.Book a free 15-min intro

## Who it’s for

- SaaS, e-commerce and services businesses in the UAE, Gulf, UK, Europe, Africa, Singapore, Latin America and India selling to US customers.

- Startups raising from US investors, who usually expect a Delaware C-Corp.

- Freelancers and agencies who want a US entity for contracts and payments — see US LLC for freelancers.

## LLC or C-Corp?

| LLC | C-Corp | 

Best for | Owner-run businesses, services, e-commerce | Startups raising venture capital, issuing stock options | 

Usual state | Wyoming or Delaware — see Delaware vs Wyoming | Delaware — see C-Corp vs LLC | 

Key annual filings for foreign owners | Form 5472 with a pro forma 1120 for a single-member LLC; state annual tax or report | Federal corporate return; Delaware franchise tax and annual report | 

## How it works

01
### Structure
A short call on your business, owners and home-country tax — so the US entity fits with your local company and personal tax.

02
### Form & EIN
State filing, registered agent, operating agreement or bylaws, and an EIN from the IRS — no SSN or ITIN needed. See EIN for non-residents.

03
### Bank & compliance
US bank or fintech account, bookkeeping set-up and a calendar of every federal and state deadline.

## Staying compliant

- Form 5472: foreign-owned single-member LLCs must file it each year with a pro forma Form 1120; the penalty for missing it is USD 25,000 per form — see Form 5472 guide.

- Delaware: corporations file an annual report and pay franchise tax by 1 March; LLCs pay an annual tax by 1 June — see Delaware franchise tax.

- Home country: your own country may tax or require reporting of a foreign company you own — we flag this at the structuring stage, and work with your local adviser.

- Full calendar: US company compliance calendar.

## Frequently asked questions
Can a non-resident form a US company?
Yes. Non-US citizens and residents can form an LLC or corporation in any US state, usually Delaware or Wyoming, without visiting the US, and obtain an EIN from the IRS without an SSN or ITIN.

Should a foreign founder choose an LLC or a C-Corp?
An LLC usually suits owner-run service or e-commerce businesses; a Delaware C-Corp suits startups raising from US investors or issuing stock options. Home-country tax rules also matter.

What annual filings does a foreign-owned US LLC have?
A foreign-owned single-member LLC files Form 5472 with a pro forma Form 1120 each year (penalty USD 25,000 per missed form), plus its state's annual report or tax.

Do you help founders outside India?
Yes — founders and companies in the UAE, Gulf, UK, Europe, Africa, Singapore, Latin America and elsewhere, working remotely.

Sell-side due diligence

# Vendor due diligence in India — getting ready for a foreign buyer

When a foreign buyer or investor looks at an Indian company, their due diligence team will find the gaps. If you find them first — and fix or explain them — you keep control of the story, the timetable and the price.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 15 October 2026·5 min read

Prepare for your deal
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- Find and fix the gaps before the buyer does — it protects price and timetable.
- FEMA filings on past foreign investment are a common trap; regularise early.
- Prepare a clean data room and a short vendor due diligence report.

## Why do vendor due diligence?

- Fewer surprises: late discoveries are what lead to price cuts, bigger escrows and tougher warranties.

- Faster deals: a prepared data room and a clear report shorten the buyer’s work.

- Time to fix: many issues — late FEMA filings, unreconciled GST, missing approvals — can be regularised before the deal, but not in the last week.

## What to review before the buyer does

Area | What to have ready | 
Financials | Audited accounts reconciled to management accounts; normalised EBITDA with one-offs explained; working capital trends | 
Tax | Income-tax assessments and pending demands; TDS defaults; GST returns reconciled with books; transfer-pricing files | 
FEMA / RBI | Every foreign investment, loan and remittance reported on time (FC-GPR, FC-TRS, FLA, ECB); late filings regularised before the buyer finds them | 
Company law | Share capital history, registers, board and shareholder approvals, charges and annual filings up to date on MCA | 
Related parties | List of transactions with promoter-linked entities, arm’s-length support, and plans to end or formalise them | 
Contracts and people | Key customer and supplier contracts, change-of-control clauses, ESOPs, labour compliance | 

## The FEMA trap

Foreign buyers pay particular attention to past foreign-investment filings, because gaps can delay closing and may need regularisation with the RBI. Check every past foreign round and transfer: was the filing made, on time, at a compliant price? See FC-GPR, FC-TRS and the draft FEMA Foreign Investment Rules 2026.

## Building the data room

- Three years of audited accounts, tax returns and GST returns, with reconciliations.

- Corporate records: incorporation documents, registers, minutes, MCA filings and charges.

- FEMA filings and RBI acknowledgements for every foreign investment, loan and transfer.

- Material contracts, licences, property documents and insurance.

- A short vendor due diligence report summarising findings and how each was resolved.

The buyer’s view of the same exercise: due diligence checklist · financial red flags.

## How we help

We run vendor due diligence for Indian companies preparing for a foreign buyer or investor, fix what can be fixed — FEMA regularisation, GST reconciliations, overdue filings — and help build the data room and answer the buyer’s questions. See fundraising and deal support and FEMA & RBI compliance.

## Sources

- Reserve Bank of India — FEMA reporting (FIRMS portal)
- Ministry of Corporate Affairs
Aerospace or defence parts? Supplier due diligence for aerospace and defence in India.
Importing coffee, rubber or wood products into the EU? EUDR and Indian suppliers: what you need by 30 December 2026.

## Frequently asked questions
What is vendor due diligence?
Due diligence commissioned by the seller (or the company raising money) before a buyer's review — to find and fix or explain issues in financials, tax, FEMA filings, company law and contracts, and to present a clean data room.

Why should an Indian company do vendor due diligence before a foreign deal?
Because foreign buyers' due diligence will find gaps — especially in FEMA filings, tax and related-party transactions — and late discoveries lead to price cuts, larger escrows and delays. Many issues can be regularised if found early.

What do foreign buyers check most closely in Indian companies?
Normalised earnings and working capital, tax exposures, FEMA compliance on past foreign investment, related-party transactions, company-law filings and key contracts with change-of-control clauses.

Forensic & fraud

# 12 warning signs of fraud in your Indian subsidiary

Most frauds in overseas subsidiaries are found late, because head office sees only summarised numbers. These are the patterns that show up first in the data and in behaviour — and the safe way to respond when you see them.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 15 October 2026·5 min read

Confidential first call
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- Watch purchasing, cash, related parties and payroll first — that's where most frauds show.
- Several signs together justify a closer look; don't confront before evidence is secured.
- Commission an independent investigation on the ground, with counsel involved where needed.

## The warning signs

# | Area | What you may see | 
1 | Purchasing | New vendors created and paid quickly; vendors sharing a bank account, address or phone with an employee; invoices just under approval limits | 
2 | Purchasing | Prices consistently above market for the same items; one vendor winning every quote | 
3 | Sales | Revenue spikes at quarter-end followed by credit notes or returns; customers nobody at head office has heard of | 
4 | Receivables | Old balances that keep being ‘about to be collected’; write-offs approved locally | 
5 | Cash and bank | Frequent cash withdrawals; payments to individuals described as ‘advances’; bank accounts head office didn’t know about | 
6 | Related parties | Rent, services or materials bought from companies linked to local management | 
7 | Payroll | Headcount in payroll higher than seen on site; PF and ESI contributions not matching payroll | 
8 | Inventory | Stock losses explained as ‘damage’ or ‘scrap’ with weak documentation; scrap sold for cash | 
9 | Expenses | Round-number consultancy, ‘liaison’ or ‘facilitation’ payments — a bribery warning sign | 
10 | Controls | One person controls vendor creation, approval and payment; audit points repeated year after year | 
11 | Behaviour | Local managers resisting visits, delaying data or insisting on handling auditors themselves | 
12 | Reporting | Monthly numbers that are always on budget, or explanations that change each time | 

One sign alone is rarely proof. Several together — especially in purchasing, cash and related parties — justify a closer look.

## Quick checks head office can run

- Vendor master vs public records: check new vendors’ GST and company registrations, addresses and directors — see how to verify an Indian company.

- Bank details: look for the same bank account across vendors and employees.

- Payroll vs PF: compare payroll headcount with provident-fund contributions.

- Related parties: compare directors of the subsidiary’s top vendors and customers with local management.

## What to do — and what not to do

- Don’t confront first. Alerting the people involved can lead to deleted records and lost evidence.

- Bring in counsel early if bribery or a regulatory disclosure may be involved (FCPA, UK Bribery Act or similar).

- Secure the data: accounting system access, bank statements, email and key documents.

- Commission an independent investigation on the ground — see forensic audit & fraud investigation in India.

- Fix the controls afterwards: vendor creation, approvals, bank mandates and monthly reporting — see subsidiary compliance.

## Sources

- Institute of Chartered Accountants of India — Forensic Accounting and Investigation Standards
UK group with India operations? Failure to prevent fraud: what it means for your India operations.

## Frequently asked questions
What are the common signs of fraud in an Indian subsidiary?
Common signs include new vendors paid quickly or linked to employees, prices above market, quarter-end revenue spikes reversed by credit notes, frequent cash withdrawals, related-party purchases, payroll headcount not matching provident-fund records, poorly documented inventory losses, and round-number 'facilitation' payments.

What should a foreign parent do if it suspects fraud in its Indian subsidiary?
Avoid confronting the people involved first, involve counsel early where bribery or disclosure may be at issue, secure the accounting, bank and email data, and commission an independent forensic investigation on the ground before fixing controls.

Can head office detect fraud in an Indian subsidiary remotely?
Partly. Checking new vendors against public company and GST records, comparing bank details across vendors and staff, and matching payroll to provident-fund contributions can surface warning signs, but confirming fraud usually needs a forensic investigation on the ground.

Forensic audit

# Forensic audit & fraud investigation in India — find out what really happened

When numbers don’t add up — a whistleblower email, unexplained cash leakage, a supplier nobody has met, or doubts after an acquisition — a forensic audit establishes the facts from the books, the bank trail and the people. We work for boards, foreign parents of Indian subsidiaries, investors and lenders.

Confidential first call
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Talk it through first — free. Book a 15-minute intro call with Durgesh to scope your requirement, timeline and fee.Book a free 15-min intro

## When you need a forensic audit

- A whistleblower complaint or an anonymous email alleging fraud or bribery.

- Margins, cash or inventory that don’t reconcile — and nobody can explain why.

- Suspected kickbacks, fake vendors or inflated invoices in purchasing.

- Funds moved to related parties or diverted from their stated purpose.

- Doubts about an Indian business after you invested in or acquired it.

- A lender, investor or board asking for an independent forensic review.

## What we investigate

Area | Typical work | 

Procurement and vendor fraud | Vendor master checks against company and GST records, duplicate and split invoices, price comparisons, links between vendors and employees | 

Fund diversion and related parties | Bank-trail analysis, round-tripping, undisclosed related-party transactions, loans and advances to connected entities | 

Revenue and receivables | Fictitious sales, channel stuffing, credit notes after year-end, customer confirmations | 

Payroll and expenses | Ghost employees, duplicate payments, expense-claim patterns | 

Inventory and assets | Physical verification against records, shrinkage, assets used outside the business | 

Bribery and third parties | Payments to agents, consultants and intermediaries; links to public officials | 

## How an engagement works

01
### Scope in confidence
A call with you — and your lawyers, where needed — to agree the allegations, the questions and who must not be alerted.

02
### Preserve and analyse
Secure books, bank statements, email and records; analyse transactions, match them to public records and test patterns.

03
### Interview and report
Interviews where appropriate, then a written report of facts, evidence and amounts — clear enough for a board, a court or an insurer.

We follow the Forensic Accounting and Investigation Standards issued by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India, and work with specialist partners for digital forensics where devices need to be imaged. Legal advice and any proceedings stay with your lawyers; we often work under their instruction.

## For foreign parents of Indian subsidiaries

US, UK and European groups need facts from their Indian subsidiary to decide on disclosure, discipline and remediation under the FCPA, the UK Bribery Act and similar laws. We investigate on the ground in India and report in English, in a form your counsel can use. See India’s anti-bribery law for foreign companies and Indian subsidiary compliance.

Before you buy, a forensic lens on the target is often cheaper than an investigation after: transaction due diligence · red flags in Indian company financials.

Guide: 12 warning signs of fraud in your Indian subsidiary.

## Frequently asked questions
What is a forensic audit in India?
A forensic audit examines a company's books, bank trail, records and people to establish whether fraud, diversion of funds or other misconduct occurred, and to quantify it — producing evidence-based findings for a board, investor, lender, insurer or court.

How is a forensic audit different from a statutory audit?
A statutory audit gives an opinion on whether financial statements are true and fair. A forensic audit investigates specific allegations or risks in depth — tracing transactions, matching records to third-party data and interviewing people — to establish facts and amounts.

Can you investigate our Indian subsidiary for a foreign parent?
Yes. We investigate on the ground in India and report in English, typically working with the parent's counsel so the findings support decisions under the FCPA, the UK Bribery Act or similar laws.

Is a forensic investigation confidential?
Yes. Scope, access and communication are agreed with you — and your lawyers where needed — so that the people involved are not alerted before evidence is secured.

Supply-chain compliance

# UFLPA and Indian suppliers — a traceability checklist for US importers

Many US companies moved sourcing to India partly to reduce China exposure. But the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act looks at where inputs come from, not just where the final product is made. If an Indian supplier uses cotton, polysilicon, aluminium or other materials that trace back to Xinjiang, the shipment can still be detained.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 15 October 2026·5 min read

Check your Indian supplier
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- UFLPA presumption (since 21 June 2022) follows inputs — Indian-made goods can be caught.
- Ask for bill of materials, input invoices, import records and production records.
- Verify against Indian import, GST e-way bill and company records, plus a plant visit.

## The rule in brief

- The Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (UFLPA) was signed on 23 December 2021. Since 21 June 2022, US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) presumes that goods made wholly or partly in Xinjiang, or by entities on the UFLPA Entity List, are made with forced labour and cannot be imported.

- The importer can overcome the presumption only with clear and convincing evidence — which in practice means supply-chain tracing documents.

- The presumption follows the inputs. A finished product made in India is covered if a covered input is used anywhere in its supply chain.

## Where Indian supply chains carry exposure

- Textiles and apparel: imported cotton, yarn or fabric.

- Solar: polysilicon, wafers and cells inside modules assembled in India.

- Aluminium, PVC and other materials sourced from Chinese suppliers, and electronics components.

## What to ask your Indian supplier

- A bill of materials showing each significant input and its supplier.

- For each input: the supplier’s name and country, purchase invoices and import records (bills of entry).

- Mill, refinery or smelter declarations for raw materials such as cotton, polysilicon and aluminium.

- Production records linking those inputs to your orders (batch or lot traceability).

- Confirmation that no supplier in the chain is on the UFLPA Entity List — and the evidence they checked.

## How to verify it in India

- Match documents to records: Indian import records (bills of entry), GST e-way bills and purchase registers should line up with the declared inputs and quantities.

- Visit the plant: see the raw-material store, check batch records and labels, and confirm capacity matches the volumes invoiced.

- Check the supplier itself: registration, filed accounts, ownership and related parties — see India Company Check and supplier verification.

- Repeat: re-check when the supplier changes its input sources, and at least once a year.

## Selling to Europe too?

The EU Forced Labour Regulation will apply from 14 December 2027 and works differently — it bans products made with forced labour from the EU market regardless of origin. The same traceability evidence will help. See due diligence for European companies.

## How we help

We visit Indian suppliers, collect and test the traceability documents against Indian import, GST and company records, and give you an English report you can keep on file for CBP. We are Chartered Accountants, not customs lawyers — your trade counsel decides what to submit to CBP. See due diligence for US companies.

## Sources

- U.S. Customs and Border Protection — Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act
- U.S. Department of Homeland Security — UFLPA Entity List
Importing coffee, rubber or wood products into the EU? EUDR and Indian suppliers: what you need by 30 December 2026.

## Frequently asked questions
Does the UFLPA apply to goods made in India?
Yes, if any input in the supply chain was made wholly or partly in Xinjiang or by an entity on the UFLPA Entity List. The presumption follows the inputs, so Indian-made goods using such inputs can be detained by US Customs.

What documents should an Indian supplier provide for UFLPA?
A bill of materials, supplier details, purchase invoices and import records for each significant input, raw-material origin declarations, production records linking inputs to your orders, and evidence that no supplier is on the UFLPA Entity List.

How can a US importer verify an Indian supplier's traceability claims?
By matching the supplier's documents against Indian import records, GST e-way bills and purchase registers, visiting the plant to check raw-material stores and batch records, and checking the supplier's registration, accounts and ownership.

Choosing an adviser

# Big 4 or a smaller firm for due diligence in India? How to choose

Foreign companies often assume due diligence in India needs one of the big international networks. Sometimes it does. Often — for partner checks, supplier verification and mid-size deals — a focused, partner-led Chartered Accountant team is quicker and better matched. Here is an honest way to decide.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 15 October 2026·5 min read

Talk through your deal
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- Big 4 or large networks fit large, multi-country or IPO-linked deals, or where a lender requires them.
- Partner-led CA firms often fit partner, supplier and mid-size deals — faster, focused, fixed fee.
- Ask who does the work, what's in scope, whether they visit, and for a sample report.

## Which fits, by type of deal

Situation | Big 4 / large network | Smaller CA-led firm | 
Large acquisition or IPO-linked deal | Usually a Big 4 or large network — lenders, boards and auditors often expect it | Can support as a second opinion or on specific workstreams | 
Multi-country deal with global reporting | Big 4 or large network, for one team across countries | Can handle the India workstream for a global lead adviser | 
Mid-size investment or JV in India | Possible, but fees and partner time may not fit the deal size | Often a good fit: partner-led, India-focused, faster to start | 
Distributor, supplier or agent checks | Rarely needed | A good fit: fixed scope, quick, with site visits | 
First check on an unknown Indian company | Not needed | A good fit: a fixed-fee company check | 

## When a Big 4 or large network is the right call

- Your lender, insurer, board or auditor requires a named large firm.

- The deal spans several countries and needs one coordinated team.

- The target is large or listed, with complex accounting, or the deal is linked to an IPO.

## When a smaller, partner-led firm fits better

- The deal or contract is mid-size and you want the senior person doing the work, not just signing it.

- You need people on the ground fast — site visits, meetings with the promoter, checking local records.

- The scope is focused: a partner, distributor, supplier or a specific tax or FEMA question.

- You want a fixed fee and a plain-English report.

## Questions to ask any adviser

- Who exactly will do the work, and who will I speak to?

- Have you checked companies in this sector and state before?

- What is in scope — and what is not (for example legal title, environmental, IT)?

- Will you visit the premises and meet management?

- What will the report look like? Ask for a sample — ours: sample report.

- Is the fee fixed, and what would change it? See what due diligence costs.

## Where we fit

We are a Chartered Accountant-led team based in Ahmedabad, with offices in Mumbai, Bengaluru, Rajkot and Dubai. We do partner, supplier and mid-size investment due diligence for foreign companies, and work alongside your lawyers and, where needed, a larger firm. Start with an India Company Check (USD 249) or partner due diligence.

## Sources

- Institute of Chartered Accountants of India
Comparing advisors? How to choose an advisor in India: checklist for foreign companies.

## Frequently asked questions
Do I need a Big 4 firm for due diligence in India?
Not always. A Big 4 or large network makes sense for large or multi-country deals, IPO-linked transactions, or where lenders or boards require a named large firm. For partner, distributor and supplier checks and many mid-size investments, a partner-led Chartered Accountant firm in India can be faster and better matched to the deal.

What should I ask a due diligence firm in India?
Who will do the work, their experience in the sector and state, what is in and out of scope, whether they will visit the premises and meet management, what the report looks like, and whether the fee is fixed.

Can a smaller firm work alongside a Big 4 on a deal?
Yes. A local CA-led team can take a specific India workstream — such as site visits, FEMA history or tax exposures — while a large firm leads the overall deal.

Korean manufacturers and their suppliers have deep roots in India — from autos and electronics to steel and chemicals — and a new wave of partners is following. ## Why companies from here use us

- Korean groups and their tier-1 and tier-2 suppliers keep adding Indian vendors, distributors and joint-venture partners.

## Your home-country rules — and what they mean for an Indian partner

- Korea’s foreign bribery law: enacted in 1998 to implement the OECD Anti-Bribery Convention, it criminalises bribing foreign public officials. A company can be liable for bribery by its intermediaries unless it exercised due care and supervision, and Korean authorities treat a genuine, operating compliance programme as relevant when assessing a company’s culpability. Recent cases show enforcement through third parties.

- What that means in India: documented checks on Indian agents, distributors, customs brokers and JV partners — who owns them, whether they deal with government bodies, and how they are paid. See promoter background checks and India’s own anti-bribery law.

## The India side

- The India–Korea Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) has applied since 1 January 2010.

Pricing

# How much does due diligence in India cost? Three levels, explained

The right level of checking depends on what you are risking. A one-off order needs a different check from a joint venture or an acquisition. Here are the three levels we offer, what each costs, and what drives the price.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 15 October 2026·5 min read

Get a quote
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- India Company Check: USD 249 fixed, report in 5 working days.
- Partner/supplier verification and full financial due diligence are quoted after scoping.
- Cost drivers: size, entities, years, record quality, site visits, timeline and report format.

## Three levels of due diligence

Level | Question it answers | What’s included | Cost and time | 
1. India Company Check | Is this company real, registered, filing, and roughly what it says it is? | Public records, filed accounts, GST, charges, directors, payment-details match, red-flag conclusion | USD 249 fixed per company · 5 working days | 
2. Partner / supplier verification | Can I trust this distributor, supplier or JV partner with money, IP or my brand? | Level 1 plus site visit, references, ownership and promoter background, anti-bribery questions | Quoted after a short call — depends mainly on location and depth | 
3. Financial, tax & FEMA due diligence | Should I invest in or buy this company, and at what price and terms? | Quality of earnings, working capital, debt, tax exposures, FEMA history, related parties, deal recommendations | Scoped quote — depends on size, number of entities, years reviewed and data-room quality | 

Start with Level 1 when you are about to pay an advance, sign a distribution agreement or shortlist suppliers. Move to Level 2 or 3 when the money, exclusivity or reputation at stake is larger. Order an India Company Check.

## What drives the cost of full due diligence

Driver | Why it matters | 
Size and complexity | Revenue, number of entities and locations, group transactions | 
Years reviewed | Usually two to three years plus the current year | 
State of the records | A clean data room is faster; scattered records add time | 
Site visits | Number of sites and how far they are from our offices (Ahmedabad, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Rajkot) | 
Timeline | Tight signing deadlines need more people at once | 
Reporting format | A short red-flag memo costs less than a full report in an investor or lender template | 

## How to keep the cost down

- Agree the scope first: list your three biggest worries (for example tax exposure, customer concentration, FEMA compliance) and focus the work there.

- Ask the target for a data room before work starts: audited accounts, tax returns, GST returns, loan papers and key contracts. See the document checklist.

- Stage it: a company check first, and full due diligence only if the first results are clean.

- Use public data: much can be checked from MCA, GST, court and credit records before you need management time — see credit checks and financial red flags.

What a full report looks like: sample due diligence report (illustrative).

## Sources

- Ministry of Corporate Affairs — company records
- GST portal — search taxpayer

## Frequently asked questions
How much does it cost to check an Indian company?
Our India Company Check costs USD 249 per company, with a written English report within 5 working days. It covers registrations, filed accounts, GST, charges, directors, payment-details matching and a red-flag conclusion.

How much does financial due diligence in India cost?
It is quoted after scoping, because the cost depends on the target's size, number of entities, years reviewed, the state of its records, site visits and the timeline. Staging the work — a company check first — keeps costs down.

How long does due diligence in India take?
A company check takes about 5 working days. Partner and supplier verification with a site visit usually takes one to three weeks, and full financial due diligence typically several weeks, depending on how quickly the target shares documents.

Manufacturing in India

# Setting up a manufacturing plant in Gujarat — a guide for foreign companies

Gujarat is one of India’s most industrialised states, with ports, industrial estates and new clusters from semiconductors at Dholera to chemicals, engineering and building materials. Here is the order of work for a foreign manufacturer, from company set-up to the first production run.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 15 October 2026·6 min read

Plan your Gujarat plant with us
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- Order of work: subsidiary → site → single-window approvals and pollution consents → factory licence → GST and payroll → production.
- Check land title and local contractors before paying advances.
- We work from Ahmedabad and Rajkot, reporting to the parent in English.

## The order of work

Step | What’s involved | Notes | 
1. Entity | Incorporate an Indian subsidiary (or JV company); file FC-GPR within 30 days of issuing shares | India entry | 
2. Site | GIDC industrial estate, a private industrial park, or a special investment region such as Dholera; check title, land use, and access to power and water | Title and encumbrance checks | 
3. Approvals | Apply through Gujarat’s Investor Facilitation Portal (single window); building plan approval; consent to establish from the Gujarat Pollution Control Board | Before construction | 
4. Before production | Consent to operate (GPCB), factory licence, fire safety, and labour registrations | Before the first shift | 
5. Tax set-up | GST registration for the Gujarat plant; import–export code; customs set-up for imported machinery; accounting system and TDS | GST advisory | 
6. People | Payroll, PF and ESI, professional tax, and contract-labour compliance | Subsidiary compliance | 
7. Suppliers | Check local vendors and contractors before advances and long-term contracts | Supplier verification | 
8. Incentives | Check eligibility under the state industrial policy and central schemes; claims depend on meeting conditions and timelines | Get eligibility confirmed in writing | 

## Why companies choose Gujarat

- Ports and logistics: west-coast ports for exports to Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

- Industrial estates: a large network of GIDC estates and private parks with ready plots and utilities.

- Clusters: chemicals and pharma, engineering around Rajkot, ceramics at Morbi, textiles, and new electronics and semiconductor projects at Dholera and Sanand.

- Recent moves: in October 2026 Gujarat and Scotland signed a cooperation MoU on renewable energy, trade and investment, and German building-materials group Knauf announced a further €350 million for Indian plants, including one in Gujarat.

## Where foreign manufacturers lose time

- Land title: agricultural land needs conversion for industrial use. Check title, conversion and encumbrances before paying.

- Consents in the wrong order: pollution “consent to establish” must come before construction, and “consent to operate” before production.

- Local contractors: advances to civil and machinery contractors are where money disappears. Check them first.

- Imported machinery: customs classification, duty and GST credit need planning before the shipment lands.

## How we help, from Ahmedabad

Our head office is in Ahmedabad, and we have a Rajkot office in the Saurashtra engineering belt. We set up the Indian company, run accounts, GST, payroll and compliance, check local suppliers and contractors, and report to the parent in English. See CA in Ahmedabad and your team on the ground in India.

## Sources

- Gujarat Investor Facilitation Portal
- Gujarat Industrial Development Corporation (GIDC)
- Gujarat Pollution Control Board
- DeshGujarat — Gujarat and Scotland sign MoU (23 Oct 2026)
- Lokmat Times — Knauf to invest €350 million in Indian plants

## Frequently asked questions
How does a foreign company set up a factory in Gujarat?
Usually by incorporating an Indian subsidiary, securing industrial land (GIDC estate, private park or special investment region), applying for approvals through Gujarat's single-window Investor Facilitation Portal, obtaining pollution consents from the Gujarat Pollution Control Board and a factory licence, and registering for GST, payroll and labour compliance before production.

Can a foreign-owned Indian company buy industrial land in Gujarat?
An Indian company with foreign investment can generally acquire land needed for its business, subject to state land laws; many manufacturers take allotted plots in GIDC estates or private industrial parks. Title and land-use checks are essential.

What is the Gujarat Investor Facilitation Portal?
The state government's single-window portal for investors to apply for and track the main state approvals needed to set up and run a business in Gujarat.

FEMA update

# Draft FEMA (Foreign Investment) Rules 2026 — what changes for foreign investors

On 21 July 2026 the Reserve Bank of India published a full draft to replace the rules that govern foreign investment in Indian companies and LLPs. Consultation closed on 31 August. Here is what would change — and why today’s deals still run on the 2019 rules.

By CA Durgesh Chavda·Last reviewed 15 October 2026·6 min read

Talk to us about your India investment
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Key takeaways
- Draft released 21 July 2026; comments closed 31 August; not yet notified as of 24 October.
- Would replace the NDI Rules 2019 — which still apply to every deal today.
- Key changes: 10% FDI line for listed and unlisted, 'foreign controlled entity', one pricing standard, investor-side compliance, easier gifts and pledges.

## Status at 24 October 2026

- Draft only. The Foreign Exchange Management (Foreign Investment) Rules, 2026 were released for comments on 21 July 2026 (RBI press release 2026-2027/726), with a deadline of 31 August 2026.

- When notified in the Gazette by the Ministry of Finance, they would replace the FEM (Non-debt Instruments) Rules, 2019. We have not seen a final notification as of 24 October 2026.

- Until then, the NDI Rules 2019 apply — including today’s pricing, reporting and deferred-consideration rules. Structure current deals on the existing rules, and build in flexibility for the change.

## Key proposed changes

Topic | NDI Rules 2019 (in force) | Draft FI Rules 2026 | 
Who can receive foreign investment | Separate categories (Indian company, LLP, investment vehicles…) | One term — “eligible investee entity” — covering companies, LLPs, SEBI-registered investment vehicles, and registered partnership firms and proprietary concerns | 
What counts as equity | Equity shares, and fully, compulsorily and mandatorily convertible debentures and preference shares, and share warrants | Instruments classified as equity under accounting standards; mandatorily convertible instruments with a fixed conversion ratio and price qualify | 
FDI vs portfolio investment | Any investment in an unlisted company is FDI; in a listed company, 10% or more | 10% or more = FDI; below 10% = portfolio investment — listed or unlisted | 
Foreign-controlled companies | “Foreign owned and/or controlled company” (FOCC) tests | “Foreign controlled entity” — ownership and control follow the sectoral regulator’s rules or the entity’s governing law | 
Pricing | Different rules for issues and transfers; some transfers exempt | One arm’s-length standard for issues and transfers (certified by a Chartered Accountant, SEBI-registered merchant banker or cost accountant); SEBI rules for listed companies; rights issues exempt | 
Who is responsible | Mainly the Indian investee company | Also the foreign investor — and, on transfers, both transferor and transferee | 
Gifts of shares | 5% cap, USD 50,000 a year, prior RBI approval | Caps and approval removed; gifts between individuals must be to close relatives; repatriation-basis gifts within LRS limits | 
Pledge of shares | Limited by who can pledge, to whom and why | Non-residents and foreign-controlled entities can pledge equity without those limits | 
Listing abroad | Separate framework | Direct listing on international exchanges codified in the Rules (Annexure I) | 

The FDI policy itself would sit in an annexure, with DPIIT interpreting it and RBI administering the rules and issuing operational directions.

## What the draft leaves open

Commentators have flagged points the draft does not address, including:

- Deal mechanics: deferred consideration, escrow and indemnity holdbacks.

- Convertible notes for startups and how convertible instruments are valued.

- Anti-dilution and assured-return features common in PE and VC deals, under a fair-value pricing standard.

- Immovable property acquisition by non-residents, which the NDI Rules cover.

## What it means for foreign investors now

- In due diligence, keep checking past compliance against the NDI Rules — FC-GPR and FC-TRS filings, pricing certificates and sectoral caps. Gaps found now are cleaned up under today’s rules. See FC-GPR and FC-TRS.

- In documents, add a change-in-law clause for deals that will close or have later tranches after the new rules are notified — especially if they use deferred consideration, escrows or convertible instruments.

- Investors under 10% in unlisted companies would be treated as portfolio investors under the draft — check what that means for your reporting.

- Responsibility shifts to investors too — keep your own record of each investment’s compliance.

All 2026 changes in one place: India FDI & FEMA updates 2026. Help with filings: FEMA & RBI compliance.

## Sources

- Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas blog — Draft FI Rules 2026: hits and misses
- CorpLawUpdates — RBI releases draft FEMA (Foreign Investment) Rules, 2026
- Reserve Bank of India — press releases

## Frequently asked questions
What are the draft FEMA (Foreign Investment) Rules 2026?
A draft released by the RBI on 21 July 2026 for public comment (to 31 August 2026) that would replace the FEM (Non-debt Instruments) Rules, 2019 governing foreign investment in Indian companies, LLPs and investment vehicles.

Are the FEMA Foreign Investment Rules 2026 in force?
Not as of 24 October 2026 — they are a draft. The NDI Rules 2019 continue to apply until the new rules are notified in the Gazette.

How would the draft rules define FDI?
Foreign investment of 10% or more in the equity of a company or LLP would be FDI, and below 10% portfolio investment — whether the company is listed or unlisted.

Do the draft rules change gifts of Indian shares to non-residents?
Yes. The draft drops the 5% cap, the USD 50,000 annual limit and prior RBI approval; gifts between individuals would be limited to close relatives, and repatriation-basis gifts to LRS limits.

Due diligence in India

# Due diligence in India for Singapore companies and investors

Singapore is one of the largest sources of foreign investment into India — through holding companies, funds and regional headquarters. Before you invest in, buy or partner with an Indian business, we check it on the ground and report in English.

Discuss your Indian partner
hello@durgeshchavda.com

Talk it through first — free. Book a 15-minute intro call with Durgesh to scope your requirement, timeline and fee.Book a free 15-min intro
Key takeaways
- Singapore is one of the largest sources of FDI into India.
- India can tax gains on Indian shares acquired from 1 April 2017 under the amended treaty.
- Singapore's PCA (s.37) reaches citizens' corrupt acts abroad — check Indian third parties.

## Why companies from here use us

- Singapore holding companies and funds invest across Indian tech, manufacturing, logistics and real estate — each deal needs India-side checks.

- Regional headquarters in Singapore often manage Indian distributors, suppliers and subsidiaries from a distance.

- Same working day: India is two and a half hours behind Singapore.

## Your home-country rules — and what they mean for an Indian partner

- Singapore’s Prevention of Corruption Act: section 37 lets Singapore treat corrupt acts by its citizens outside Singapore as if done in Singapore — so how your Indian agents and partners win business matters.

- Investor and lender expectations: Singapore-based funds and banks expect documented know-your-counterparty checks on Indian investees and partners.

- Tax: under the 2016 protocol to the India–Singapore tax treaty, India can tax gains on shares of Indian companies acquired on or after 1 April 2017. Treaty benefits also need a tax residency certificate, Form 41 and real substance in Singapore.

## The India side

- The India–Singapore Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement (CECA) has applied since 2005.

- Setting up or restructuring: India for Singapore companies · Singapore holding companies · reverse flips to India.

- Before you invest: financial red flags · credit checks.

## What we check for you in India

- Identity, registrations and filed financial statements of the Indian partner — how it works.

- Financial, tax and FEMA review; related parties; litigation through public records and counsel.

- Promoters, directors, government links and how intermediaries are paid — for your anti-bribery and supply-chain files.

- Premises visits from Ahmedabad, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Rajkot or Dubai, with a written report in English.

- Full scope: partner due diligence · investment due diligence · supplier verification.

We are Chartered Accountants, not lawyers: home-country legal advice on compliance programmes stays with your counsel. Our reports are built to slot into their files.

## Sources

- DPIIT — FDI statistics
- Singapore Statutes Online — Prevention of Corruption Act 1960
- Income Tax Department — India–Singapore DTAA

## Frequently asked questions
Who can do due diligence on an Indian company for a Singapore investor?
CA Durgesh Chavda's team checks Indian targets, partners and suppliers for Singapore companies and funds — records, financials, tax, FEMA, promoters and premises — and reports in English.

Are capital gains on Indian shares taxable for Singapore companies?
For shares acquired on or after 1 April 2017, yes — the 2016 protocol to the India–Singapore treaty gives India the right to tax those gains. Shares acquired earlier were grandfathered.

Does Singapore's anti-corruption law apply to bribery in India?
Section 37 of Singapore's Prevention of Corruption Act lets Singapore prosecute its citizens for corrupt acts committed abroad, so due diligence on Indian agents and partners is a sensible safeguard.
